sections.title: Fuzzy matching
sections.summary: Index and rank fuzzy matches for titles, IDs and branches.

requirements.text: Build a pure search index from the loaded Trace: one entry per PRD section, spec section or task, retaining its existing Node identity. Index section titles and IDs and task titles and branch names; no server endpoint, persisted index or new contract field is needed.

Trim the query and match case-insensitively. Support ordered subsequences for abbreviations and a single insertion, deletion, substitution or adjacent transposition for query tokens of at least four characters; shorter tokens require exact, prefix or subsequence matches. Every whitespace-separated query token must match within one indexed field. Rank exact field matches first, then prefixes, contiguous matches, typo matches and subsequences; within a match class prefer titles, then IDs, then branches, then prose. Break remaining ties by score, source order and stable node key.

Return one result per node with its best matching field, score and sorted, non-overlapping, half-open UTF-16 ranges in the original visible text. Case normalization must preserve a mapping back to source positions and never split a surrogate pair. An empty query returns no search results. The same trace and query always produce the same order.

Cache the index by searchable trace content and rebuild it only when that content changes. Query changes reuse the index; status-only refreshes do not trigger markdown parsing. Keep matching and result derivation pure and use installed Effect core APIs. No search dependency is selected or added by this plan.

tests.text: Results have unique node identities, deterministic order and valid non-overlapping source ranges; normalized matches never split surrogate pairs.
Exact titles outrank fuzzy titles; abbreviations and one-edit typos match; blank and unmatched queries, punctuation and mixed-case Unicode are covered.

sections.title: Search controls and chain highlighting
sections.summary: Add search navigation and temporary chain highlighting.

requirements.text: Add window-local query and active-result state to the Schema-defined Model, with fact-named messages for query edits, result navigation, result selection and clearing. The pure update function derives results and reconciles the active node after trace refresh: retain it if still matched, otherwise choose the first result or none. Query edits reset to the first result; empty and unmatched queries have no active chain.

Render a labelled toolbar search input, result count and ranked result list showing kind, title and matched field. Use accessible combobox/listbox semantics with an active descendant, ArrowUp/ArrowDown navigation bounded at the list ends, Enter to select, pointer selection, and Escape to clear. Handle these keys only in the search control; they must not reach the reader's own keys, such as Escape. Announce the count and no-results state without stealing focus.

Selecting a result brings it into view in the reader. For a PRD section, the PRD pane scrolls to its heading. For a spec section or a task, the first PRD section of its chain, in document order, is the current section for as long as the result is active, ahead of the pin and without changing the pin or the PRD pane's scroll; its card, row and chip scroll into view in their own panes, and a result in a spec section's prose shows that card open while it is active. A spec section that implements no PRD section has no card to go to: selecting it opens it in the detail panel, the one case where a result opens the panel. Keep keyboard focus in search. Preview its chain as a hover does. Only the active result contributes a search chain; never union separate result chains into a synthetic chain.

Mark direct text matches with semantic mark nodes and a separate node outline, in PRD headings and prose, spec card headers, summaries and full sections, task rows and chips; related chain members get chain highlighting but no text marks unless they independently match. Hover remains the top preview, above search. Draw a curve as part of a chain only when both endpoints belong to that same chain. Use text labels or outlines as well as colour to identify the active result.

Clearing search removes its marks, outline, results and temporary chain while preserving the pinned section, the detail panel, document content and task state. The current section goes back to the pin or to the section at the top. A no-results query shows a message without dimming the panes. Pinning a section and opening a task continue to work. Keep the existing markdown lazy boundaries effective when queries change.

tests.text: Type an abbreviation or typo, navigate with arrows, select with Enter and pointer, and assert matching text, active result and connected-chain highlighting.
Search, hover and a pinned section coexist; clearing and Escape preserve the pin and the detail panel; zero matches leave the panes usable; refreshed and removed results reconcile correctly.

Select a spec section and a task whose PRD section is not the pinned one: its PRD section is current while the result is active and the pin comes back when the search is cleared; unrelated curves stay unlit. Select spec.format, which implements no PRD section, and find it open in the detail panel.

sections.title: Prose search and inline highlights
sections.summary: Search markdown prose with snippets and inline match highlights.

requirements.text: Extend the index to visible PRD and spec prose, owned by the nearest preceding section heading until the next heading of any level; nested sections own their text and do not duplicate it in their parent. Extract paragraphs, list items, table cells, link labels and inline code from the markdown AST. Exclude HTML/comments, heading ID attributes, link destinations, code fences and Mermaid content; diffs and session logs remain out of scope.

Keep a visible-text-to-AST-text-node offset map for each searchable prose block. Match within a paragraph, list paragraph or table cell, including across emphasis, links and inline code, but not across block or section boundaries. Reuse the fuzzy ranking and source ranges from fuzzy-matching; prose ranks below titles within a match class. Return one result per node, with its best match and a bounded context snippet from the matching block.

Render match ranges as semantic mark nodes in snippets and in document text leaves, splitting ranges across existing inline elements while preserving formatting, safe links, text selection and heading IDs. Do not rewrite source markdown, inject HTML or wrap DOM after rendering. Highlight the best matching field or prose block per result consistently with its snippet. For typo matches, mark the matched source word; for subsequences, mark matched characters.

Parse each changed document once and share its AST and position mapping between indexing and rendering. Query edits only rematch and render marks. Reconcile results and offsets when source content changes. Selecting a prose result brings the matched block into view, falling back to the owning section until block measurement is available; keep code highlighting and diagram mounts stable.

tests.text: Highlighting preserves the original visible text and every range maps to text in its owning section.
Find prose spanning bold text and a link, inspect the highlighted snippet and inline marks, select the matching block, and clear without losing formatting or pins.
Nested sections, inline code, tables, escaped markdown and Unicode retain correct offsets; comments, code fences and diagram labels do not match; query changes reuse the parsed AST.

sections.title: Curves
sections.summary: Specifies the curves that join the three panes for the current section: pure links and paths from measured rectangles, held inside their panes, measured by one Mount and lit along a chain on hover.

requirements.text: Curves are drawn for the current section only: one from its heading to each of its spec cards' headers, and one from each task row, a stray's too, to that task's chip.
`linksOf(cards)` is pure and returns those pairs as keys; each element a curve can end on carries its key in `data-wire`.
`wiresOf(links, boxes, panes)` is pure and returns, for each link with both ends measured, a Wire with its two keys, its path and `isOffPane`.
A curve runs from the middle of its source's right edge to the middle of its target's left edge; the PRD end leaves from the right edge of the PRD pane, level with the heading.
Each end's height is held inside its own pane, 8px in; a spec, row or chip end that had to be moved makes its curve `isOffPane`, and the PRD end does not count.
The path is a cubic bezier whose control points sit level with its ends, max(20, half the horizontal distance) in from each, computed by the reader itself.

A Mount on the reader body measures every `[data-wire]` element and the three panes at most once per animation frame, sends `MeasuredWires` only when a rectangle changed, and measures on mount, on a scroll in any pane, on a window resize, when a ResizeObserver on a pane or its content fires, and when `data-wires` changes.
`wiresView` is one fixed SVG over the reader body with no pointer events and `aria-hidden`; an `isOffPane` wire is dashed and fainter.
The PRD body and each card are lazy views, so a measurement renders the SVG again and nothing else.

A card's header, a task row and a chip send `HoveredNode` on pointer enter and focus and `LeftNode` on leave and blur; the hovered node's chain is drawn in ink and thicker, and every card, row and chip outside it is dimmed.

sections.title: Stacks
sections.summary: Lays the stacks pane out like the spec's stack diagram: one numbered box per stack, a chip per task bottom to top inside it, and the boxes in rows over the base branch by what they wait on, with the current section's tasks standing out.

requirements.text: `stacksOf(tasks)` is pure, replaces `stackLayoutOf`, and returns the stacks in number order, each with its number, root, area, level and cells.
A root is a task whose parent is null, names no task or would close a cycle; every other task belongs to its parent's stack, so each task is in exactly one stack.
Stacks are numbered from 1 in TaskIdOrder of their roots and labelled `Stack N · area`, the area being the second segment of the root's first spec section ID, or `Stack N` when it has none.

A task's row in its box is its depth along parent links, so a chain has no gaps; columns in a box are numbered depth first, the first child by ID continuing its parent's column and each other child starting the column after those its elder siblings use, so the columns under any task are one unbroken run.

A stack's level is 1 when it waits on no other stack, otherwise one more than the highest level among the stacks it waits on; a dependency that names no task or closes a cycle between stacks is ignored.

The view draws every stack whatever the current section is: the levels bottom to top, each a row of its stacks in number order aligned to the bottom, over a bar labelled with the base branch that is sticky at the bottom of the pane and is not a node; the pane starts scrolled to the bottom.
A stack is a box with `data-stack`, its number in a corner, `labelOf(stack)` as its title and aria-label, and a CSS grid of its cells, only as tall as its deepest chain.

A task is a chip: a button with `data-task` and `data-wire`, a status dot and the ID, a title and aria-label with the ID, title, branch, worktree and status, and a `--blocked` border when gated; it sends `ClickedTask`.
A chip in the current section's chain has `data-current`, an ink border and a hard shadow, and so does its box; every other chip is at 45% opacity and still takes focus, hover and clicks.
Over the diagram, sticky at the top: "N of M stacks hold this section · X of Y tasks done" and a legend.

Inside each box a solid arrow runs from each parent to each child, a finished trunk folds into one segment and each fork's columns are labelled; a task's dependencies on other stacks are dashed arrows drawn only for the task in focus.

sections.title: Boxes, forks and finished trunks
sections.summary: Defines the pure `boxOf` function that works out what a stack's box draws before it is drawn: depth-first columns, spans centred over forks, a finished trunk that folds into a segment, fork labels from spec sections, and the keys parent arrows run between. It also defines the trunk's label text.

requirements.text: `boxOf(stack, tasks, isUnfolded)` in `apps/viewer/src/boxes.ts` must be pure and must work out what a box draws before the box is drawn.
`stacksOf` in `packages/core/src/stacks.ts` must number a box's columns depth first, following the rule in `spec.viewer.stacks`, so that the columns under any task form one unbroken run.
A task's `span` must be the number of columns used by the task and everything built on it in the box, so a task at a fork spans its children's columns and is drawn centred under them.
A box's trunk must be `trunkOf(stack, tasks)` from `links.ts` when that trunk holds two or more tasks. A trunk of one task stays a chip, so the box has no trunk.
A box without a trunk must be the same whether it is folded or not.
A trunk must be folded unless `isUnfolded` is true.

When the trunk is folded, the trunk's tasks must have no cell and every other task's row must drop by the trunk's length, so the children of the trunk's last task are in row 1, standing on the segment under the grid.
When the trunk is unfolded, every task must keep the row `stacksOf` gave it.

A fork is a task with two or more children in the box. Each child of a fork must be labelled with the last `.`-separated part of its first spec section, for example `fuzzy-matching` for `spec.viewer.fuzzy-matching`.
A child of a fork that has no spec section must not have a fork label.
When a fork is the last task of a folded trunk, its children must keep their fork labels.
`endKeyOf(box)(id)` must return `segment:<root>` for a task inside a folded trunk and `task:<id>` for any other task.
A parent arrow's source must be the parent's `endKeyOf` key.
A parent arrow's target must be `fork:<id>` for a labelled child, so the arrow ends at the foot of the label, and `task:<id>` for any other child.
Parent links between tasks inside a folded trunk must not draw an arrow.
A box's `arrows` must hold one arrow for each parent link drawn, each of kind `parent`.

`trunkLabelOf(stack, trunk)` must return the trunk's first and last IDs joined by an en dash, then the stack's area, then the count of done tasks, separated by ` · `, such as `t45–t52 · viewer · 8 done`, leaving out the area for a stack with none, such as `t45–t52 · 8 done`.

decisions.text: Columns are numbered depth first, replacing the old rule that numbered them by the ID of each column's first task.
decisions.why: The old rule breaks the unbroken run of columns under a task: in Stack 8 of this repo, t55 sits between t106 and its child t115.

decisions.text: Only a trunk of two or more tasks counts as a trunk; a trunk of one task stays a chip.
A trunk is folded by default and unfolded only when `isUnfolded` is set.
A labelled child's parent arrow targets `fork:<id>` rather than the child's task key.

sections.title: Drawing a box
sections.summary: Draws a stack's box as a grid of chip rows and gap rows, with fork labels under labelled children and a segment button that folds and unfolds the box's trunk. Folded tasks are found through their segment by links, curves and scrolls, and fold state lives only in the window.

requirements.text: `stackView` draws the box returned by `boxOf(stack, trace.tasks, isUnfolded)`.
Each chip row of a box is two grid rows: the chips' row and, under it, a gap row `--stack-gap` (22px) tall that the arrows into the row above cross.
In a box of `rows` rows, a chip in row `r` is placed in grid row `2 × (rows − r) + 1` and in the grid columns `column / span <span>`, centred in them.
Box grid columns are at least a chip wide, with 12px between them.
A labelled child's fork label is a `span` with `data-fork-label` and `data-wire` holding `fork:<id>`, placed in the gap row under the child's chip and across its columns, in the `label` style.

A box with a trunk has a native button under its grid, as wide as the box, with `data-segment` holding the root, `data-holds` holding the trunk's task IDs separated by spaces, `data-wire` holding `segment:<root>`, and `aria-expanded`.
A folded segment shows a done dot and `trunkLabelOf`, and its `title` and `aria-label` add "click to unfold".
An unfolded segment is a slim bar under the chips reading `Fold <first>–<last>` (for example `Fold t45–t52`).
Clicking the segment, folded or unfolded, sends `ClickedSegment({ root })`.
`reader.unfolded` is a `Record<TaskId, boolean>` keyed by trunk root and is empty at first, so every trunk starts folded.
`ClickedSegment` flips the unfolded state of its root.
Folding or unfolding a trunk must not send a command or a presence message.
Fold state must not be stored in the URL.
A folded segment has `data-current` when it holds a task of the current section.
A folded segment has `data-faded` when a section is current and the segment holds none of its tasks.
A folded segment has `data-selected`, drawn with an ink outline, when it holds the task open in the detail panel.
A folded segment has `data-dimmed` when a node is hovered and the hovered chain holds none of its tasks.
A folded task has no chip, so wherever the reader looks for a task's chip it finds the segment holding that task instead.
`linksOf` takes the key function, and a curve from a task row ends on `endKeyOf` of its task.
The scrolls that look for `[data-task="<id>"]` in the stacks pane, for a search result in `reader.ts` and for a link step in `links.ts`, also match `[data-holds~="<id>"]`.
The body's `data-wires` attribute also lists the unfolded roots, so `MeasureWires` measures again after a fold changes the pane.

sections.title: Parent arrows
sections.summary: Draws parent arrows between the chips, fork labels and segments of the stacks list: a pure `arrowsOf` computes each arrow's end points and bezier path from the rectangles `MeasureWires` already measures, and `arrowsView` renders them as an SVG overlay under the chips.

requirements.text: Arrows are measured by `MeasureWires`: every chip, fork label and segment carries a `data-wire` key, so `MeasuredWires` holds their rectangles.
The stacks list carries `data-wire="stacks:list"`, and its rectangle is the origin the arrows are drawn from.
No second measuring mount is added for the arrows.
`arrowsOf(links, boxes, origin)` is a pure function.
For each link with both ends measured, in link order, `arrowsOf` returns an `Arrow` with its keys, its kind, its `from` and `to` points and its SVG path, in coordinates relative to `origin`.
When the target is above the source, the arrow leaves the middle of the source's top edge and arrives at the middle of the target's bottom edge.
When the target is below the source, the arrow leaves the middle of the source's bottom edge and arrives at the middle of the target's top edge.
When source and target overlap in height, the arrow joins the middles of their facing sides.
An arrow's path is a cubic bezier whose control points carry on in each end's direction, `max(8, half the distance along that direction)` out from that end.
A marker draws the arrow's head at its `to` point.
`arrowsView(arrows, h)` renders an SVG placed over `.stacks-list`, which is `position: relative`.

A spec section shows its ID, summary, key chips, tasks as rows that add to the trail, and its judgments; each judgment shows its question, verdict, message and the probability or label and confidence behind it.

sections.summary: Every place the reader and the code view can open gets a deep link written with `LinkFromPath`. The section covers resolving a link against the trace and loaded data, opening it with the address bar and history kept in sync, and a "Copy link" action on every step. The canvas screen has no links.

requirements.text: Every place the reader and the code view can open must have a link, written with `LinkFromPath`.
Resolving a link must check its steps against the trace and the loaded data, and must say which step is missing when one is.
Opening a link must apply its steps the same way clicks would.
Opening a link must keep the address bar and the browser history in step with the screen.
Every step must offer a "Copy link" action that copies that step's link.
While the canvas screen is open, the viewer must not write a link and must leave the address as it is.
A link must always open on the reader or the code view, never on the canvas screen.

artifacts.name: LinkFromPath
artifacts.description: Writes the link for a place the reader or the code view can open; defined in `spec.contract.links`.

decisions.text: The canvas screen has no links: while it is open the viewer writes no link and leaves the address unchanged, and links only open on the reader or the code view.

sections.title: Resolving a link
sections.summary: Defines the pure `resolveLink` function that checks a deep link's steps in order against the trace and loaded data. It returns what opened, what is still waiting for data and what is missing. It also defines the `linkNoticeView` status notice that tells the reader how far a link opened and why it stopped.

requirements.text: `resolveLink(trace, link, loaded)` must be pure, where `loaded` holds the patches and sessions the model has received.
`resolveLink` must check each step of the link in order and return `resolved`, `waiting` and `missing`.
`resolved` must list the steps that open, each with what it needs: a passage step comes with its mark ranges and a diff step comes with its route path.
`waiting` must be the index of the first step whose data is not loaded yet, or none.
`missing` must hold what did not resolve. At most one miss stops resolution, and passage misses do not stop it.
A miss must have the shape `{ index, step, reason, message }`.
A section step must resolve when a section in `trace.prd` or `trace.spec` has its ID. Otherwise it gives `section-missing`, meaning the section was deleted.
A passage step must resolve when its section resolves and the quote is found in it. Otherwise it gives `passage-changed`, which does not stop resolution, and the step opens as its section.
A task step must resolve when `trace.tasks` has the task, and give `task-missing` otherwise.
A stack step must resolve when `stacksOf(trace.tasks)` has a stack with that root, and give `stack-missing` otherwise.
A segment step must resolve when that stack's finished trunk holds two or more tasks, and give `segment-missing` otherwise.
A diff step must resolve when `head` is one of the preceding task's commits. Otherwise it gives `commit-not-on-task`, meaning the branch was restacked or rewritten after the link was copied.
A commit step must resolve when a task in the trace has the commit and, when a task precedes the step, that task is the preceding one. Otherwise it gives `commit-missing` or `commit-not-on-task`.

A file step must resolve when the patch of the diff or commit before it is loaded and has the path. Otherwise it gives `patch-unavailable`, carrying the fetch error or the demo's missing patch, or `file-not-in-diff`.
A lines step must resolve when the file's hunks show every line from `start` to `end` on that side, and give `lines-not-in-diff` otherwise.

A turn step must resolve when a commit in the trace has the session, the session is loaded and it has a turn with that ID. Otherwise it gives `session-missing`, `sessions-unavailable` in the demo, or `turn-missing`.
A note step must never resolve yet and must give `notes-unavailable`, because notes are not stored yet.
A step whose patch or session is not in `loaded` must set `waiting` to that step's index, and resolution must stop there until the data arrives.
`trunkOf(stack, tasks)` must start at the stack's root and take the run of `done` or `landed` tasks up to the first fork or the first unfinished task.
Resolution must turn a patch into file names and hunk line ranges with the same patch-to-files step the diff view uses.
Resolution must not parse a patch in a second way, separate from the diff view's patch-to-files step.

`passageOf(index, section, quote)` must find a passage in the prose blocks its section owns. The blocks and their visible-text offset maps come from the prose index, where nested sections own their own text.
When matching a passage, the blocks' visible texts must be joined with one space and each run of whitespace collapsed to one space.
The first exact, case-sensitive match of the quote must count as the passage.
A passage match must be mapped back to a range in each block it covers.
An edit anywhere else in the document must leave the passage's ranges pointing at the same text, and an edit inside the passage must remove the match.
`linkNoticeView` must sit under the top bar of the reader and of the code view, with `role="status"`.
The notice must say how far the link opened and what is missing, for example: "Opened as far as task t74. `packages/cli/src/api.ts` is not in that diff."
For a passage miss the notice must read: "The passage changed: "…first 80 characters…" is no longer in Viewer."
A link that does not decode must open nothing, and the notice must show its `LinkError`, for example: "This address is not a Cairn link: step 3 (file) must follow a diff or a commit."
The notice must have a "Dismiss" button that sends `ClickedDismissLinkNotice`.
The next link that opens must replace the current notice.
The window must never be blank after a link opens: at worst it shows the reader with no steps, under the notice.

A link that does not decode opens nothing but still leaves the reader with no steps under the notice, never a blank window.

sections.title: Opening a link
sections.summary: Makes the viewer a Foldkit application that owns the URL: a single `linkRoute`, `linkOf` to derive the canonical link from the model, `openLink` to apply a link's steps the way clicks would, and `withAddress` to keep browser history in step so Back walks a link one step at a time.

requirements.text: The viewer must become a Foldkit application that owns the URL.
`route.ts` must define `linkRoute` as the viewer's only route, over `LinkFromPath`.

If Foldkit's route combinators can express a list of steps that print and parse from one definition, `linkRoute` must be built from them, with each argument's schema taken from the contract. Otherwise `linkRoute` must be one wildcard path run through `LinkFromPath`, and that Schema stays the single definition.
URL changes must arrive as the `ChangedUrl` message, and `pushUrl` and `replaceUrl` must be commands.
A link must carry no host, so it opens the same way under `pnpm dev`, under `cairn serve` and on the demo site.
Vite, the server and the demo site must each answer any path that is not a file with the viewer's page.
The model must gain `reader.maybePassage`, `reader.maybeFocus`, `maybeLines` on the `Code` screen, `maybeHead` on `WholeTask`, `maybeLinkNotice` and `maybePendingLink`.
When `maybeHead` on `WholeTask` is None, the code view must show the task's newest commit, as before.

`linkOf(model)` in `links.ts` must be pure and must give the canonical link of what was opened, in this order: the pinned PRD section or a PRD passage in its place; a spec passage; the focused stack or segment; the detail trail's steps, each a `section` for a spec section or a `task`; a `task` step for the code view's task when that task is not the trail's last step; a `diff` with the head it shows, or a `commit`; the selected file, then `lines`; the highlighted turn.
A link must not hold the section at the top of the PRD pane, pane widths, the models switch, card density, cards opened by their header or the search. Each viewer keeps those.

`openLink(model, link)` must resolve the link and clear what a link holds (the pin, the passage, the focus, the trail and the code view selection). It must then apply each resolved step the way the click it stands for does.
Opening a PRD section step must pin that section.
Opening a spec section step must start the detail trail on it, or add it to the trail when the panel is open.
Opening a PRD passage step must pin its section and mark the passage.
Opening a spec passage step must pin the first PRD section the spec section implements if the pinned section is not one it implements. It must then open the card in `opened` and mark the passage.
A spec section that implements no PRD section must open in the detail panel, as search does.
Opening a task step must start or extend the detail trail.
Opening a stack or segment step must set the focus. The focused box must get `data-linked` and an ink outline, and for a segment its trunk's chips must get them too.
Opening a diff step must open the code view on the trail's last task at `head`.
Opening a commit step must open the code view on that commit. If the trail's last task is a different task, the commit's task must be added to the trail first.
Opening a file step must select the file.
Opening a lines step must set `maybeLines`.
Opening a turn step must open the code view on the session's newest commit if no code step came before it, then highlight the turn as `ClickedTurn` does.
Passage marks must be `mark[data-link-passage]` nodes, placed by the same range splitting that search marks use.
Passage marks must have an ink underline and no fill, so a search mark inside one still shows.
The diff mount must gain a `data-lines` attribute, such as `n40-42`. Its `MutationObserver` must read the attribute to scroll to those lines and select them.
Line selection must use `@pierre/diffs`' line selection if `CodeView`'s declarations have one. Otherwise it must draw a line annotation, as the turn marks do.

For each step past the longest prefix the old link and the new link share, `openLink` must return a scroll command that brings the step into view, whether that is a heading, a passage's first mark, a card, a chip or a box.

`openLink` must return a fetch for each patch or session the steps need that is not loaded, through the requests the code view already makes. This is how a link opened in a new window loads its diff and its turn.

When `ReceivedPatch` or `ReceivedSession` arrives for `maybePendingLink`, the link must be resolved again. A step that is now missing must be taken out of the state, its notice must be shown, and the address must be replaced with `replaceUrl(linkOf(model))`.
A path that fails to decode with a `LinkError`, or a link with a step that `resolveLink` cannot find in the trace, must show the link notice.
`withAddress(update)` must wrap the viewer's update.

On first load, `init` must decode the URL into `maybePendingLink`. The first trace must open the link, and the history must be rewritten with one entry per step: `replaceUrl` with the first step, then `pushUrl` for each longer prefix.
A `ChangedUrl` from Back, Forward or a typed address must open that link without writing history.
A `ChangedUrl` whose link equals `linkOf(model)` must do nothing. This also absorbs the echo of the viewer's own `pushUrl`.

After any other message, if `linkOf` changed, the new link must be pushed. Pinning, opening a task or a spec section, cutting or shortening the trail, Escape, opening the code view, selecting in its tree, selecting lines, highlighting a turn and "Back to the plan" must each become one history entry.
Escape with the panel closed must also clear the focus, as it unpins.

sections.title: Copying a link
sections.summary: Adds copy-link buttons across the viewer (PRD headings, spec cards, passages, the detail trail, stack boxes, the code view, diff lines and session turns). The buttons copy the same deep link the address bar holds, or a shorter link that opens one step on its own. The section also defines the pure `aloneOf` function in `links.ts`, which builds that shortest link.

requirements.text: Copying the address bar must copy the deep link. The copy-link buttons must give the same link text without navigating to it.
`aloneOf(link, index)` in `links.ts` must be pure. It must return the shortest link that opens the given step by itself.
For `aloneOf`, a section, passage, task, stack, segment, commit, turn or note step must be its own step, so the link holds only that step.
For `aloneOf`, a diff step alone must be its task plus the diff.
For `aloneOf`, a file step alone must be the diff or commit before it plus the file. For a diff, the diff's task comes first.
For `aloneOf`, a lines step alone must be the steps that the file needs, then the file, then the lines.
`copyLinkView({ path, label }, h)` must render a small `btn`. Clicking it must send `ClickedCopyLink` with the path.
On `ClickedCopyLink`, the update must run a Command that writes `location.origin` plus the path to the clipboard and then sends `CompletedCopyLink`.
After `CompletedCopyLink`, the copy-link button must read "copied" until the next render, as the section ID button does.
A PRD heading must have a "Copy link" button beside its section ID button that copies `/section/<id>` alone.
The pinned PRD section's status line row must copy the link up to that section's step.
A spec card header must have a "Copy link" button that copies the section alone.
The `TrackSelection` subscription in `subscription/selection.ts` must listen to `selectionchange` and handle it at most once per animation frame.
When both ends of the selection lie in one `[data-passage]` element, `TrackSelection` must send `SelectedPassage` with the section and the quote.
A PRD section's prose wrapper must carry its section ID in `data-passage`. A spec card's full section body must too.
The passage quote must be the selection's text, trimmed, with whitespace collapsed.
When the selection leaves a `[data-passage]` element, `TrackSelection` must send `ClearedPassageSelection`.

While a passage is selected, the section's status line row (in the PRD) or the card header (in the spec) must show "Copy link to passage". Clicking it opens the passage as a step, which pins the section and marks the passage, and copies the link up to that step.
When the selected passage is over 500 characters, the "Copy link to passage" button must be disabled, with the title "Select at most 500 characters to link to them."
In the detail panel, each step of the trail must have a "Copy link" button that copies the path up to that step.
The detail panel's heading must copy its task or spec section alone.
In the stacks pane, each box must have a "Copy link" button in its corner that copies `/stack/<root>`.
A stack box whose finished trunk holds two or more tasks must also have "Copy link to finished trunk", which copies `/segment/<root>`.
The code view top bar must have "Copy link", which copies the whole path.
The code view top bar must have "Copy alone", which copies `aloneOf` its last step. That step is the lines when lines are selected, and otherwise the file, the diff or the commit.

The diff mount must turn a line selection into `SelectedDiffLines` with the side, start and end. It uses the line selection callback of `@pierre/diffs`, or a click listener on the line-number gutter if the library has no such callback.
A line selection must join the current link.
In the session pane, an opened turn must have "Copy link", which copies the path up to that turn.
A link to lines copied from a task's diff must carry the `diff` step's head: the commit the code view showed when the link was copied. The link then opens on the same code after more commits land.

sections.title: List items
sections.summary: Makes list items that carry an ID behave in the viewer like small sections inside their section. Each such item gets a coverage annotation and a copyable ID. Items can be hovered, pinned and linked from spec cards and task rows, and their coverage counts toward the section's own counts.

requirements.text: `renderMarkdown` strips a trailing `{#id}` or `{#}` from a list item.
A list item with an ID gets `data-item` and `data-wire="prd:<id>"`, and ends with the `itemAnnotation` hook.
An item's annotation is a native button showing a status dot followed by counts such as `1 spec · 2/7 tasks`, taken from `countsOf(trace, id)`.
An item that nothing maps to shows `nothing maps to this` in place of the counts.
An item's ID is a small button that shows on hover and on focus within the item, and copies the ID on click through `ClickedSectionId`.
`chainOf(trace, section)` includes the chains of the items under the section.
A heading's status line and its section's cards count the whole section, including its items.
`HoveredNode` on an item's annotation lights the item's chain: its cards, their task rows and its chips.
`linksOf` adds a curve from an item to each of its cards.
`ClickedItemAnnotation` pins the item in `maybePinned`.
`currentOf` returns a pinned item. The spec pane then shows only that item's cards, and the stacks light only its tasks.
Clicking a pinned item's annotation again unpins it, and so does pressing Escape when no panel is open.
A card's `Implements` chips that name a PRD section or item are buttons that send `ClickedImplementsChip`.
`ClickedImplementsChip` scrolls the PRD pane to the item or heading and sets `reader.maybeMarked`. The element then has `data-marked` until the next click or hover elsewhere.
Hovering a task row or a chip gives `data-marked` to the items it builds.
The detail panel's "Traces to" list shows each of the task's items with the title of the section it is in, e.g. `prd.cli.lint · in CLI`.

sections.title: Cost on the graph
sections.summary: Adds API-equivalent cost estimates and allowance usage to the viewer: pure helpers in cost.ts (compactOf, cardCostOf, allowanceOf) and their display in the detail panel, task rows and card headers. It also covers narrow-width and keyboard behaviour.

requirements.text: cost.ts is pure.
compactOf(usage) returns a label like `API est. $0.42` when the estimate is complete.
compactOf(usage) returns a label like `API est. $0.42 · partial` when the estimate is partial.
compactOf(usage) returns `Usage unavailable` when there is no usage or no priced call.
compactOf never returns a `$0` label.
cardCostOf(tasks) sums share × estimate over distinct (session, task) pairs.
In cardCostOf, a session referenced twice is counted once.
In cardCostOf, a shared session counts only its share.
cardCostOf states coverage in the form `1 of 2 tasks priced`.
allowanceOf(tasks) sums attributable percents only within the same allowance and the same resetsAt.
allowanceOf keeps each allowance's label.
The detail panel shows a `Usage and cost` block below model and reasoning and before the commits and code.
The `Usage and cost` block's summary line shows the API-equivalent estimate and the attributable allowance consumed.

Expanding the `Usage and cost` block with disclosureView lists each session with its purpose and share, the actual models and reasoning per session, and the token categories. It also lists billed cost when known, allocated subscription cost when configured, each rate's source and date, the assumptions and exclusions, and the coverage.
Account-wide allowance in the detail panel sits under its own `Account (all use)` label.
Account-wide allowance is never added to the task's figures.
In a task row, the compactOf label follows the model chip as a button that sends ClickedCostEstimate, which opens the task's detail with the cost block expanded.
The detail state's isCostOpen holds whether the cost block is expanded.
Selecting the task's chip opens the same detail as the cost button.
The card header shows the cardCostOf total, with its coverage when the total is partial.
The card header has a disclosure listing the contributing tasks and sessions.
The spec pane never adds card cost totals together.
Percentages always carry their allowance's label, such as `3% of codex-pro weekly`.
Task rows are a size container.
Below 380px row width, the cost moves to a second line under the title, and the title, model and status stay on the first line.
Every cost label is visible text and every detail is reached through a button or a disclosure, so nothing depends on hover.

sections.title: What depends on what
sections.summary: Adds dependency links to the viewer: each heading and item shows how many sections it needs and how many need it, plus how many of its tasks are ready. A links button opens a list under the heading of what it needs, what needs it, and its next tasks. The task detail panel gains a `Needed by` list and says whether a pending task can start.

requirements.text: The reader must get section links by calling `sectionLinksOf` on the index it builds from the trace.
A heading's status line and an item's annotation must end with the counts of what it needs and what needs it, in the form `needs 3 · needed by 1`.
A section with unfinished tasks must add the number of tasks ready to start, such as `2 ready`, or `waiting` when none can start.
The links part of the status line or annotation must be its own button, sending `ClickedLinks`, separate from the pin button.
`reader.maybeLinksOpen` must hold the one section whose links list is open.
Clicking the links button of the open section again must close its links list.
Escape must close the open links list. It does so after an open panel has gone back and before a pin is cleared.
Opening a links list must not pin the section.
`linksView` must sit under the heading and show three groups: `Needs`, `Needed by` and `Next`.
The `Needs` group must list each section or item that is needed, with its status dot and the task pairs that link them, such as `t95 needs t94`.
The `Needed by` group must list each section or item that needs this one, with its status dot and the task pairs, the same way as `Needs`.
The `Next` group must list the section's unfinished tasks in build order with ready tasks first. Each task that is not ready shows what it waits on, such as `waits on t94`.
Clicking a section or item entry in the links list must send `ClickedLinkedSection`, which scrolls the PRD to that section or item and marks it.
Clicking a task entry in the links list must send `ClickedTask`.
Hovering an entry in the links list must send `HoveredNode` for that entry, which lights its tasks in the stacks.
A `switchView` labelled "Everything before and after" must set `reader.isLinksTransitive`. When it is set, the links lists show the transitive dependencies in build order.
The task detail panel must list `Needed by` beside the task's parent and dependencies.
For a pending task, the task detail panel must say `Can start now`, or `Waits on` followed by the tasks it waits on, such as `Waits on t94, t95`.

sections.title: Command menu
sections.summary: Builds a ⌘K-style command menu for the viewer in Foldkit: a modal dialog opened by ⌘K/Ctrl+K, `/` or the toolbar search button. It lists commands, tasks, and PRD and spec matches ranked by the same fuzzy search index as the toolbar search. It also has nested search pages, keyboard navigation, chain preview and an accessible combobox/listbox view.

requirements.text: The command menu must rank results with the fuzzy search index, so that the menu and the toolbar search box never disagree.
`menuKeys.ts` must listen to `keydown` events on the document.
⌘K on macOS, or Ctrl+K on other platforms, must send `PressedMenuShortcut`, which opens the menu when closed and closes it when open.
The platform must be read once, from `navigator.userAgentData` or `navigator.platform`.
Typing `/` must send `PressedMenuShortcut` only when the event's target is not an input, a textarea or editable content.
The toolbar search box must become a button showing the current query, and a click on it must open the menu.
Opening the menu must store the focused element's ID in `returnFocus`, and closing the menu must focus that element again.
`menuResultsOf(model)` in `menu.ts` must be a pure function.
With an empty query on the root page, `menuResultsOf` must list the commands, then the current section's tasks.
With a non-empty query, `menuResultsOf` must run the fuzzy search and group the results under PRD, Spec, Tasks, then Commands, in that order.
A result group with no matches must be hidden.
On a nested page (tasks, prd or spec), only results of that page's kind must be listed.
Each menu result must carry its kind, its title and its matched ranges, and a task result must also carry its status and ID.

The menu's commands must be the viewer's existing controls: toggling models and reasoning on or off; choosing Titles, Summary or Full spec for the cards; opening the code view; copying a link to what is in view; and `Search tasks…`, `Search the PRD…` and `Search the spec…`, which open a nested page.
The open-the-code-view command must apply only when the detail panel shows a task.
The copy-link command must copy a link to what is in view by sending `ClickedCopyLink` with `linkOf(model)`.
The fold/unfold-every-finished-trunk command must not be listed until the stacks pane folds trunks. After that it must be listed.
Each command must have an `appliesTo(model)` predicate, and a command that does not apply must not be listed.
A command that has a keyboard shortcut must show the shortcut on the right of its row.
Up and Down must move `active` through the results and wrap at the ends.
Pointer movement over a result must set `active` to that result.
The active search result must preview its chain behind the menu, as the active fuzzy search result does: `currentOf` takes the menu's active result while the menu is open.
Enter, or a click on a result, must run the active result.
Running a search result must close the menu and set the search query and the active search result to it, exactly as selecting it in fuzzy search does.
Running a command must close the menu and run the command.
On a nested page, Backspace on an empty query, or Escape, must go back to the root page.
Escape on the root page must close the menu and discard the preview. The panes, the pin and the detail panel must return to how they were before the menu opened.
After a search result has run from the menu, a second Escape must clear the search, as it already does.
`PressedEscape` must reach the detail panel only when the menu is closed.
`menuView` must render a `role="dialog"` element with `aria-modal="true"`, placed over the centre of the window.
The menu's query input must have `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant`.
On a nested page, the menu must show that page's badge before the query input.
Results must be a `role="listbox"` with `role="group"` sections labelled by their headings, and `role="option"` items with `aria-selected`.
Tab and Shift+Tab must keep focus on the query input while the dialog is open.
The result list's height must follow the number of its results.
The dialog must fade and scale in over `--d-fade`, and with reduced motion `base.css` must turn that animation off.
A query with no matches must show the message `No matches for "<query>"`.

sections.title: Notes
sections.summary: Shows review notes in the viewer: a pure `notesOf` resolves each note's anchor and places it beside a PRD passage or heading, a spec card header, a task row and chip, or a diff line. Notes whose anchors don't fully resolve go into a missing list, and resolved notes are hidden unless a window-local switch is on.

requirements.text: The viewer must not let people write notes; it only shows them (writing notes in the room comes with v2).
`notesOf(trace, loaded, isShowingResolved)` in `notes.ts` must be a pure function.
`notesOf` must decode each note's anchor with `LinkFromPath` and resolve it with `resolveLink`, then place the note by the last step that resolved.
A note whose last resolved step is a passage or PRD section must show beside the heading or the passage.
A note whose last resolved step is a spec section must show beside the spec card's header.
A note whose last resolved step is a task or commit must show on the task's row and chip.
A note whose last resolved step is lines in a diff must show on that line in the diff.
A note whose anchor does not resolve all the way must be listed in the task detail when its link names a task, and under its section otherwise.
A note whose anchor does not resolve all the way must carry the missing step's message, as defined in `spec.viewer.deep-links.resolving-a-link`.
A note marker must be a small button showing the count of open notes.
Opening a note marker must show each note's kind, author, status and markdown body rendered through `renderMarkdown`, with a link that opens the note's anchor.
Task rows and chips must show the number of open notes in the form `◆ 2`.

In the diff, notes on lines must be written as JSON into the mount's `data-notes` attribute, which the mount's `MutationObserver` reads and draws as line annotations, the same way turn marks are drawn.
The task detail must list the task's notes, and each listed note must open its link.
Resolved notes must be hidden unless `isShowingResolved` is on.
A `switchView` labelled "Show resolved notes" must set `isShowingResolved`.
`isShowingResolved` must be local to the window.
Every note must be placed exactly once, either at its anchor or in a missing list.

sections.title: Effect UI
sections.summary: Moves the viewer from Foldkit 0.171.0 to Effect UI in seven steps, each passing `pnpm check`: the Effect upgrade, a gated spike, an Effect UI host over the Foldkit views, the tests, the views top down, removing Foldkit, then components.

requirements.text: `pnpm check` passes after each step of the move.
The steps run in order: Effect upgrade, spike, host, Scene tests, views, removing Foldkit, components.
No step ports a canvas view; the canvas is removed before the host step.
A view added before the host step lands is written in Foldkit, and one added after it in Effect UI.

decisions.text: The move goes in steps behind a one-way bridge rather than in one change.
decisions.why: Each pull request has to pass CI on its own head, and one change across every view and test would be too large to review.

decisions.text: The canvas is removed first.
decisions.why: Porting views that are about to be deleted is wasted work.

requirements.text: `effect` and `@effect/vitest` in the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` catalog are 4.1.6.
Every `@effect/*` package pinned at 4.1.5 in a `package.json` moves to 4.1.6 in the same change.
Only one version of `effect` is installed.
The Effect API lookup is rebuilt with `refresh-effect-api.ts` and `index-effect-core.ts`.
A breaking change in the release is fixed in this change.

requirements.text: `@effect/ui` and `@effect/ui-kit` are installed from the pkg.pr.new snapshot of one Effect-TS/ui commit, named by its short SHA.
The SHA is written once, in the `effect-ui` catalog in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and both packages use it.
Moving to a newer SHA is its own change.
Nothing the spike adds runs in the viewer.
`.agent_sources/effect-ui/index.md` points at Effect UI's `LLMS.md`, `ai-docs/src/10_ui/` and package sources at the pinned SHA, and AGENTS.md's table has an Effect UI row.
`effect-ui/controls.ts` rebuilds the switch and disclosure on `@effect/ui-kit`'s `Switch` and `Collapsible` with the same classes, roles and labels.
`foldkitView(h, html)` renders a Foldkit `Html` value as Effect UI children with the same elements, attributes, properties, classes, styles, keys and text.
A bridged event handler sends the same `Message` the Foldkit handler sends.
A Foldkit `Mount` becomes an Effect UI mount on the same element.
`EFFECT-UI.md` has one row for each Foldkit API the viewer imports, naming its Effect UI replacement or saying there is none and what the viewer does instead.
`EFFECT-UI.md` says whether the bridge works and which later step changes if it does not, and lists what was reported upstream.

sections.title: The host
sections.summary: Mounts the viewer as one Effect UI component, `Viewer`, whose update wraps today's update and whose view renders today's Foldkit views through the bridge, with the address and subscriptions on Effect UI.

requirements.text: `Viewer` is an Effect UI component with the viewer's `Model` and `Message`.
`Viewer`'s `init` is today's `init`.
`Viewer`'s `update` calls today's `withAddress(update)`, returns the new Model with `$.evolve` and runs each Foldkit Command with `$.run`.
No Message handler is rewritten in this step.

`entry.ts` mounts `Viewer` with `BrowserHost.mount` in place of `Runtime.run`.
Back, Forward and a hash change send `ChangedUrl`, and a click on an anchor sends `ClickedLink`, through `BrowserRouter`.
Each subscription becomes `Subscription.make(key, stream)` over the stream it has now.
Foldkit stays installed, and every existing test passes unchanged.

sections.title: Views

requirements.text: Views move from the top of the tree down, one part per change: frame, reader, stacks, detail and code, then markdown.
A Foldkit view never holds an Effect UI view.
A moved view keeps its classes, roles, labels, keys and Messages.
Native buttons keep `type="button"`.
Markdown moves last, once every view that renders it has moved.
A view may use an `@effect/ui-kit` component when the DOM the tests check stays the same.

sections.title: Removing Foldkit

requirements.text: Any view still on Foldkit is rewritten in Effect UI.
`update` returns `$` results itself, and the update adapter is deleted.
`modifyFields` becomes `$.evolve`, and `defineMessageUnion` and `defineTaggedUnion` become `UiSchema.TaggedEnum`.

`bridge.ts` is deleted.
`foldkit`, `@foldkit/ui`, `@foldkit/vite-plugin` and `@foldkit/oxlint-plugin` are uninstalled, and the Foldkit patch and its `patchedDependencies` entry are removed.
AGENTS.md, the Effect checklist, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and LICENSING name Effect UI instead of Foldkit.

The xstate docs index is regenerated and `AGENTS.md` gains a lookup row for model-based testing.
A model test lives in `<subject>.model.test.ts`, and its model is a machine that is never the code under test; when the code runs that machine, the test is of what the code adds around it.
A model test runs `propertyTest` in `it.effect` with a fixed seed and asserts `{ transitions: 1 }` coverage.
Events come from the model's schemas through `eventsFromSchemas` from `@xstate/test/effect-schema`, with an `override` for `Option`.

sections.title: Presence against the room machine
sections.summary: Tests the presence server over real WebSockets against the room machine, so every participant sees the machine's room.

requirements.text: The server runs `roomMachine`, so the test is of what it adds: the sockets, the broadcast to every participant and leaving when a socket closes.
The model is `roomMachine` and the system under test is `PresenceRoute` with `Room.layer` on a Node server on port 0, with real WebSocket clients.
Model IDs come from a pool of three and map to the client and server ID each joined with.
`joined` opens a client, replacing an existing one; `moved` writes a `CursorJson` frame; `left` closes the client; an event for an ID with no client does nothing.

`read` waits until every open client has the room after the last event, up to two seconds, and returns each client's room with IDs mapped back; `projectModel` returns the machine's participants once per open client.

tests.text: Every participant sees the room machine's participants, in order, after every generated join, move and leave.
Sending the room only to the participant who changed it fails the test.

decisions.text: Test the server against the machine it runs.
decisions.why: The machine's transitions have their own tests; this one checks the sockets and the broadcast the server adds.

requirements.text: The models are written from the spec sections, not from the viewer's code, and the system under test is `update` from `init` on the demo trace with the reader open.
The reader model covers starting, extending, cutting and closing the trail, Escape that steps back or unpins, and pinning by the status line.
The panes model covers arrow keys, a press, moves and releases from the pressed pointer and from another, and a move with no button held, within limits written out in the model.
Payloads come from the demo trace's IDs, and a step index from the current trail.

sections.title: Derivation against a model of its inputs
sections.summary: Tests derive against a machine of what an orchestrator writes and what git shows, which keeps facts and replays them as derive recomputes.

requirements.text: The model is a machine of one task's inputs, written from the PRD, and not the task machine.
The model keeps facts: the reports so far, whether a commit touched a gated path and whether the task landed; after each event it replays its reports from the start and carries nothing over.
`reported` lines follow the lifecycle, a gated `done` waits for a human, and a report the lifecycle does not allow adds a warning.

`committed` on a gated path gates every report of the task, earlier ones too; `merged` and `squashed` stay true and land the task from any status, with a warning for landing without approval when it is gated and its reports do not end in `done`.
`read` runs `derive` with a test `Git` Layer over shuffled event lines and returns the status and the number of warnings.

tests.text: derive agrees with the model on status and warnings after every generated report, commit and landing, whatever the order of the lines.
Letting an agent's done approve a gated task fails the test.

decisions.text: Replay the facts in the model instead of keeping a running status.
decisions.why: derive computes the gate from every commit before it replays events, and landing is git state that stays true.

sections.title: Hosted launch
sections.summary: Builds Cairn's hosted service (launching as prdddd): a single shared Cloudflare application where people sign up into their own workspace, with a Worker in front of D1, one PrdRoom Durable Object per PRD, and R2 for large revision bodies. It brings forward only the parts of the deferred v2 multiplayer architecture that the launch needs.

requirements.text: A person who visits the hosted site can sign up and then lands in their own workspace.
Signing up for the hosted service must not require the person to enter payment details, open a Cloudflare account or deploy anything.
One shared application serves every hosted workspace.
The self-hosted team offering is the same application, deployed into an operator's own Cloudflare account with billing turned off.
The local CLI, `cairn serve` and the files in `.cairn/` keep working as before and need no account.
`cairn connect` joins a repo to one hosted PRD.
The launch builds accounts, one room per PRD, D1, R2 and the Alchemy deploy, only as far as the `prd.launch` sections ask for them.

The launch must not build the parts of `prd.v2-multiplayer-on-cloudflare` that stay deferred: simultaneous text editing and Loro, carets and selections in presence, code and sessions in the room, syncing notes from `cairn.db`, attachments on comments, and remote MCP.
Requests from the browser (workspace screens and the reader), from `cairn connect` and from Stripe webhooks reach the Worker, which handles auth, policy and the HTTP APIs.
The Worker reaches D1 and a PrdRoom Durable Object, of which there is one per PRD.

D1 holds Better Auth's users, accounts, sessions and organizations, and Cairn's workspaces, document directory, grants, invitations, agents, links between PRDs, public search, usage, subscriptions and revocations. D1 is the authority for who may do what and what exists.
Each PRD room's SQLite holds that PRD's revisions, threads, comments, progress events, plan records and trace snapshots, and is the authority for the content and discussion of that one PRD.
Revision bodies over 512 KiB are stored in R2. R2 is the authority for nothing on its own: the room names each R2 object it uses.
The hosted service must never store code, diffs, session logs or model keys.
Every launch section's Done-when statement is proved by a test named in one of the launch sections, and `spec.hosted-launch.launch-acceptance` maps the release gates to those tests.

The self-hosted team offering is the same application deployed into an operator's own Cloudflare account with billing turned off, not a separate product.
Accounts, one room per PRD, D1, R2 and the Alchemy deploy are built in this section, even though `spec.scope` defers `prd.v2-multiplayer-on-cloudflare`.
decisions.why: The launch needs that part of the architecture.

decisions.text: The deferral of v2 multiplayer still covers simultaneous text editing and Loro, carets and selections in presence, code and sessions in the room, syncing notes from `cairn.db`, attachments on comments, and remote MCP.
The stores are split by authority: D1 for who may do what and what exists, each room's SQLite for one PRD's content and discussion, and R2 for nothing on its own.
Revision bodies over 512 KiB go to R2 instead of the room's SQLite.
The hosted service never stores code, diffs, session logs or model keys.

sections.title: Hosted contract
sections.summary: Defines the shared hosted contract exported from `@cairn/contract/hosted`: ID formats, principals, workspaces, membership and access, documents, revisions, discussion threads, plan records, entitlements, WebSocket room messages and error shapes that the Worker, the viewer and `cairn connect` exchange, plus regenerated JSON Schema files.

requirements.text: The Worker, the viewer and `cairn connect` must exchange the shapes defined in the hosted contract.
`@cairn/contract/hosted` must export the hosted contract shapes.
The hosted contract modules must import IDs from `../ids.ts` and `../link.ts`.
The hosted contract modules must never import from `index.ts`.
Random IDs must be 12 characters of [a-z0-9] generated with crypto.getRandomValues, after a type prefix (w_, doc_, rev_, agt_, inv_, plan_).
An EventId must be the SHA-256 hex of the events.jsonl line's bytes.
An Author's name is the name as shown; for an agent it shows "<agent name> for <person>".
A Workspace name must be 1 to 80 characters long.
Access levels are ordered read, comment, edit, manage, and `atLeast(have, need)` must answer by that order, with "none" below every level.
A workspace invitation's role must be "admin" or "member", and a document invitation's access must be "read" or "comment".
An AgentScope must list at least one document and at least one action, each action being "read", "progress" or "comment".
A Document title must be 1 to 200 characters and is metadata independent of the markdown's own heading.
A Document's memberAccess, what every workspace member has, must default to "edit".
GET /api/documents/:id must return a DocumentView: the Document plus the caller's access, the markdown and whether it has a plan.
A Revision's number must count 1, 2, ... per document and kind.
A Revision's hash must be the SHA-256 of the stored markdown's UTF-8 bytes.
A SaveInput's base may be null only for a document's first spec revision.
A content revision must never be compared with a file format's `version` field.
An Anchor's section of null means the whole document.
A Comment body is markdown of at most 20,000 characters.
In a changed AnchorState, `original` must be null for a reader who may not open the anchored revision.
Comment IDs must be NoteIds, and a thread's root comment ID must be the thread's ID.
A null value in Limits means unlimited.
Room WebSocket messages must flow server to client only; every write must go over HTTP.
Every denied read must be reported with the `not-found` HostedError code.
The JSON Schema files must be generated again, as in `spec.contract.javascript-entry`.

sections.title: Policy
sections.summary: Defines the pure `decide(facts, action)` policy function in core, the single authority on whether a person, agent or anonymous reader may perform an action. It covers document access rules, agent ceilings, the per-action allow table, and how the Worker maps a denial to 404 or 403.

requirements.text: `decide(facts, action)` in core must be a pure function.
`decide` must be the only place that determines whether a principal may act.
Every HTTP route, every room write, search, previews and live subscriptions must ask `decide` whether the principal may act.
`decide` must not allow any action that a rule does not allow.
`decide` must not take any subscription input, so a plan can never grant access.
An owner or admin of a document's workspace must have `manage` access to the document.
A member of a document's workspace must have the greater of the document's `memberAccess` and their own grant.
A person who is not a member of the document's workspace must have their grant capped at `comment`, which makes them a guest.
A public document must give everyone, including the anonymous reader, at least `read` access (the public floor).
An agent's access must be the lower of its delegating person's access, computed by the person rules, and what its scope allows.
An agent whose scope actions include `comment` must have a scope ceiling of `comment`; otherwise its ceiling must be `read`.
An agent that is revoked, or whose scope does not name the document, must have no access.
`document.read` (current revisions, threads and the plan view) must be allowed when access is at least `read`.
`document.history` (listing and opening revisions) must be allowed only when access is at least `read` without counting the public floor.
`document.export` must be allowed exactly when `document.read` is allowed.
`document.comment` must be allowed when access is at least `comment` and the principal is not anonymous.
`thread.resolve` must be allowed when `document.comment` is allowed and, for an agent, the thread's root author is that agent.
`document.edit` (save, restore, rename) must be allowed only for a person with `edit` access.
`document.manage` (visibility, grants, guest invitations) must be allowed only for a person with `manage` access.
`plan.write` must be allowed for a person with `edit` access, or for an agent with `progress` in its actions and `read` access on the document.
`progress.write` must be allowed under the same conditions as `plan.write`.
`gate.approve` must be allowed only for a person with `manage` access, never for an agent.
`workspace.read` (the PRD list, members, agents) must be allowed only for a person who is a member of the workspace.
`workspace.createDocument` must be allowed only for a person who is a member of the workspace.
`workspace.manageMembers` must be allowed only for an owner or admin of a team workspace, and changing or removing an owner must require an owner.
`workspace.billing` must be allowed only for an owner of the workspace.
`agent.create` must be allowed only for a person who is a member, for documents they can read, with actions within their own access.
Agents must not be allowed to edit or manage documents.
The Worker must turn a denied read of a workspace or document into `404 not-found` with the same body a nonexistent ID gets, so the response reveals nothing about whether the thing exists.
The Worker must turn a denied write on something the principal can read into `403 forbidden` carrying the decision's reason, such as `Only a person can approve a gate.`.

sections.title: Worker and storage
sections.summary: Builds `apps/hosted`: a single Cloudflare Worker for every workspace. It uses an Effect HTTP router, resolves each request to a principal, loads facts from D1, and keeps one `PrdRoom` Durable Object per document with its own SQLite. It also covers the D1 schema, R2 storage for large revision bodies, caching headers, the Alchemy deploy and the Workers-pool tests.

requirements.text: `apps/hosted` must be one Cloudflare Worker that serves every workspace; no workspace gets its own deployment.
The HTTP router must be Effect HTTP, served through Effect's web handler.
The installed `effect`'s declarations for the Workers entry must be read before `worker.ts` is written.
Every route must decode its input and encode its output through the hosted contract.
Better Auth's handler must be mounted at `/api/auth/*`.
The hosted viewer build must be served as Workers static assets.
Every `GET` path not handled by another route must fall back to the hosted viewer's page.
An unknown route must return a `404` in the error shape.
A request with an invalid body must get an `invalid-input` error that names the field.
`principal.ts` must resolve each request to a `Principal`. A Better Auth session cookie or a device-authorization bearer token resolves to a person.
A request with an `Authorization: Bearer cagt_…` header must resolve to an agent principal.
A request with no session cookie, device-authorization bearer token or agent bearer token must resolve to an anonymous principal.
`facts.ts` must load a request's `Facts` with one D1 query per request, run against the primary so that a decision never reads a stale replica.
The query that loads `Facts` must also return the document's `access_epoch`.
`PrdRoom` must be a Durable Object class with one instance per document, addressed by `idFromName(documentId)`.
The Worker must call `PrdRoom` through Workers RPC.
`PrdRoom` storage must be its own SQLite, used through `@effect/sql-sqlite-do`, with migrations run through `Migrator.fromRecord` the first time the instance wakes.
A room that is evicted and woken again must keep its SQLite rows.
A room migration must not be edited once it has landed.
D1 must be used through `@effect/sql-d1`. Its migrations sit in `src/d1/migrations/` and run on deploy.
Better Auth's tables must come from Better Auth's own schema.

The D1 migrations must add the tables `workspaces`, `documents`, `document_grants`, `document_invitations`, `agents`, `connections`, `usage` and `pending_revocations` with the columns the section defines.
`blobs.ts` must store a revision body larger than 512 KiB in R2 at `revisions/<document>/<revision>.md`.
R2 must be reached only through the room, so that the room's policy applies to it.
The launch must not include attachments.
Every protected response must carry `Cache-Control: no-store`.
Every public response must carry `Cache-Control: no-cache` and an `ETag`.
No shared cache may ever hold document content.
`alchemy.run.ts` must define the Worker, the `PrdRoom` namespace, the D1 database, the R2 bucket, the email binding, a cron trigger that runs every minute, and the secrets.
The secrets must be Alchemy config bindings, and none may be in the repo.

The new dependencies `better-auth`, `@effect/sql-d1`, `@effect/sql-sqlite-do`, `stripe` and the dev dependency `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` must each be pinned at the version current on the day it is added.
Tests must run in `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` with local D1, Durable Objects and R2.
The configuration docs for `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` must be read before `vitest.config.ts` is written.

sections.title: Accounts and workspaces
sections.summary: Builds sign-in on Better Auth in the Cloudflare Worker, with GitHub, Google, magic-link and device authorization. Sign-up creates a personal workspace for each new user. Workspaces sit on Better Auth's organization plugin. The section also defines a Mailer service and the `GET /api/me` and `POST /api/workspaces` routes.

requirements.text: Sign-in must run on Better Auth inside the Worker, keep its tables in D1, and be wired up through Alchemy's Better Auth integration.
Users must be able to sign in with GitHub, with Google and with a magic link.
An operator must be able to turn off each sign-in method (GitHub, Google, magic link) on its own.
A magic link must work only once.
A magic link must expire five minutes after it is issued.
A sign-in must join an existing user with the same email only when the provider has confirmed that email. GitHub, Google and a magic link to one address then reach one user.
A sign-in whose provider has not confirmed the email must not be joined to an existing user with that email.
Auth must support device authorization, for use by `cairn connect`.
Workspace membership and roles must be held by Better Auth's organization plugin. Each workspace is one organization, and a `workspaces` row adds Cairn's ID and the workspace kind.
Document grants and guest access must be implemented by Cairn itself, not by the organization plugin.
`Mailer` must be a service. Its live layer sends mail through Cloudflare Email Service from a sending subdomain of the configured domain.
If Cloudflare Email Service cannot deliver to an address, a transactional email provider must take its place behind the same `Mailer` service.
The test layer of `Mailer` must record each message sent.

Better Auth's after-user-created hook must create a personal workspace in one D1 batch. The batch holds an organization, a `workspaces` row of kind `personal` named `<name>'s workspace`, the user as its owner, and a `usage` row.
The sign-up hook must check for an existing personal workspace first, so that running it again creates nothing.
Sign-up must not ask for payment details.
Under managed billing, a newly created personal workspace must be on the free plan. With billing off, it must be self-hosted.

`GET /api/me` must return the user, their workspaces each with role and kind, and `sharedWithMe`. `sharedWithMe` lists the documents the user holds grants on in workspaces where they are not a member.
Each `sharedWithMe` entry in `GET /api/me` must carry its workspace name and nothing else about that workspace.
`GET /api/me` must return `401` when the caller is signed out.
`POST /api/workspaces` must take `{ name }` and create a team workspace on the free plan, with the caller as owner.
A personal workspace must have exactly one member.
A personal workspace must not be able to invite more members.
PRDs in a personal workspace may still have guests.

sections.title: Entitlements
sections.summary: Builds plan limits for the hosted product: plans decoded from a `PLANS` JSON binding, atomic per-dimension usage reservations that fail with `limit-reached`, an entitlements endpoint for members, and over-limit handling that only blocks new reservations.

requirements.text: Plans are configuration, not code: the `PLANS` binding is JSON decoded through the `Plans` schema.
A paid plan's member limit is the number of seats bought.
With billing off, every workspace is on the `self-hosted` plan and every limit is `null`.
Code must not depend on the free-plan numbers used in the test fixtures.
The `members` dimension counts workspace members plus pending workspace invitations, so accepting an invitation never fails on the limit.
The `prds`, `privatePrds` and `publicPrds` dimensions count the workspace's documents.
Guests and agents must not be counted as members; inviting a guest never touches `members`.
Inviting a guest checks only `guestsPerPrd`, against that document's guests.
`reserve(workspace, dimension)` runs `update usage set <dim> = <dim> + 1 where workspace_id = ? and (? is null or <dim> < ?)` and goes ahead only when exactly one row changed.
After a successful reservation the caller writes its own row; if that write fails, it releases the reservation with `- 1`.
Moving a document between private and public reserves one dimension and releases the other in one batch.

`GET /api/workspaces/:id/entitlements` returns `Entitlements` to workspace members.
After a downgrade or a lapse, `overLimit` lists every dimension whose usage is above its allowance.
The only effect of being over the limit is that new reservations in the over-limit dimensions fail.
Being over the limit must not delete anything or change visibility; editing, commenting, history and export work as before.
Policy must never read entitlements.

sections.title: Room
sections.summary: Builds the per-PRD Durable Object room that linearizes and deduplicates writes, pushes live updates over hibernating WebSockets with a state endpoint for reconnects, and the `revoke` flow that withdraws a member's, guest's or agent's access, closing their open sockets before the request returns.

requirements.text: Every write reaches the room as an RPC from the Worker, and only after `decide` has allowed it on fresh facts.
Each write RPC carries the principal, the document's `access_epoch` the Worker decided under, and a `clientId`.
The room's writes are linearized: the Durable Object handles one turn at a time.
Each accepted write gets the next `seq` from the room's own counter.
No client's clock orders any write.
The room stores each write's result in the `idempotency` table keyed by `client_id`, and a retry with the same `clientId` gets the stored result and writes nothing.
Progress events are keyed by their `EventId` and inserted into `events` with `on conflict do nothing`.
`GET /api/documents/:id/live` upgrades to a WebSocket only once the Worker has allowed `document.read`.
The room accepts the socket with the hibernation API and saves the principal, the access level, the session's expiry and the section being read in the socket's attachment.
Each write broadcasts one `RoomMessage` to every socket the write is visible to.
An anonymous socket gets messages only while the document is public, and gets the trace in its public form.
A socket whose session has expired is closed with code 4401 at its next broadcast.
`reading` messages go only to sockets with at least `comment` access; an anonymous reader neither sends nor receives presence.
`GET /api/documents/:id/state` returns the room's `seq`, the current revisions, the threads, the trace hash and the latest approvals.
A client fetches `state` whenever its socket opens, replaces what it holds, and then ignores messages whose `seq` it already has.
A client reconnects with backoff from 1 second to 30 seconds.
A reconnect loses no committed comment and repeats no event.
Removing a membership, a guest grant or an agent's delegation goes through `revoke` in `revocation.ts`.

`revoke` first, in one D1 batch, deletes the membership or grant or marks the agent revoked, increments `access_epoch` on every affected document (all of a workspace's documents for a membership, one document for a grant, the agent's scope for an agent), and inserts a `pending_revocations` row.
`revoke` then calls each affected room's `revoked({ principals, epoch })`, and the room stores `min_epoch` in its own storage so it survives hibernation.
The room refuses any write whose epoch is below `min_epoch` with `stale-authorization`, and the Worker then decides that request again once, on fresh facts.

On `revoked`, the room works out the access again from D1 for every socket of the given principals; a socket left with no access gets `{ type: "access", access: "none" }` and is closed with code 4403, and any other affected socket gets its new access.
After the room calls, `revoke` deletes the `pending_revocations` row and returns.

A revocation takes effect when its request returns: every HTTP request decided after the D1 batch reads the new facts, every room write decided before it carries an older epoch and is refused once the room has the new `min_epoch`, and a write the room accepted before then is ordered before the revocation.
If a room call fails, the revocation request still returns.
A cron trigger retries each pending revocation row every minute until every room has acknowledged it.
The UI must not claim that content already delivered to a browser can be taken back.
