decisions.text: Writes are ordered by the room's own `seq` counter, never by any client's clock.
decisions.why: A Durable Object runs one turn at a time, so the room's writes are linearized.

decisions.text: Progress events are deduplicated by their `EventId` with `on conflict do nothing`, not through the `clientId` idempotency table.
Sockets are accepted with the hibernation API, with per-socket state kept in the socket's attachment.
The room keeps `min_epoch` in its own storage.
decisions.why: So it survives hibernation.

decisions.text: On every socket open a client refetches the full `state` and replaces what it holds, instead of replaying missed messages.
decisions.why: Missed messages are covered by the fetch and retried writes by their idempotency keys, so a reconnect loses no committed comment and repeats no event.

decisions.text: A revocation request returns even if a room call fails, with a cron trigger retrying the pending row.

sections.title: Revisions
sections.summary: Stores every accepted PRD or spec edit as a numbered, durable revision in the document's room, with save, list, read and restore RPCs, stale-base rejection, and the HTTP routes that expose them to editors and history readers.

requirements.text: Every accepted PRD or spec edit must be stored as a durable revision in the room's storage.
The room's save RPC must perform all of its steps in one turn.
If a save's clientId already has a stored result, save must return that stored result.
If a save's base is not the current revision of that kind, save must fail with stale-revision, send the current RevisionBody so the person can compare it with their draft, and write nothing.
Save must run assignSectionIds on the markdown, with prd or spec as the kind, so every heading has an ID that anchors and links can name.
If the hash of the assignSectionIds result equals the current revision's hash, save must return the current revision and must not make a new revision.
Otherwise save must insert revision number + 1 with its parent set to the current revision, move current to it, update documents.current_* and updated_at in D1, and broadcast revision.
listRevisions(kind) must return the revisions of that kind newest first, without bodies.
readRevision(id) must return one RevisionBody.
Restore must be a save of the given revision's markdown with restoredFrom set to that revision.
Restore must be refused as stale like any save when its base is not the current revision.
Restore must not touch grants, threads, events, plan records or approvals.
Revision bodies over 512 KiB must be stored in R2.
A revision over 5 MiB must be rejected as invalid-input.
POST /api/documents/:id/revisions must require the document.edit policy and return 201 with the RevisionBody, or 409 when stale.
GET /api/documents/:id/revisions?kind= must require the document.history policy and return the revision list.
GET /api/documents/:id/revisions/:rev must require the document.history policy, return the revision body, and return 404 for a revision of another document.
POST /api/documents/:id/restore must require the document.edit policy and return 201 with the new RevisionBody, or 409 when stale.
A public reader must get the current revision only through GET /api/documents/:id.
A public reader must never get revision history.
Revisions must survive a room restart, a hibernation and a deploy.
Creating a document must count as its first save, producing its first revision.

sections.title: Document directory
sections.summary: Builds the workspace document directory for hosted Cairn: routes to create, import, list, find, read, rename and export standalone PRDs, each with a stable DocumentId. It also covers the browser address scheme, which keeps working after a rename and gives the same 404 for a document outside the workspace as for an unknown one.

requirements.text: A workspace holds any number of independent PRDs.
Each PRD has a stable DocumentId that does not change when its title changes.
A PRD with no spec, plan, task or repository is a complete document and supports comments and sharing.
POST /api/workspaces/:id/documents is authorized by the workspace.createDocument policy and takes { title?, markdown?, clientId }.
Creating a document reserves the prds and privatePrds entitlements.
Creating a document creates a documents row that is private with memberAccess "edit", and saves revision 1 in the new room.
When a document is created with no markdown, revision 1 is `# <title>`.
A new document's title is the title given, else the first level 1 heading of the imported markdown, else `Untitled PRD`.
GET /api/workspaces/:id/documents?q= is authorized by workspace.read and returns the workspace's documents, newest change first, filtered by title ignoring case when q is given.
GET /api/documents/:id is authorized by document.read and returns the DocumentView: the current PRD markdown, the caller's access, and whether a plan exists.
PATCH /api/documents/:id is authorized by document.edit and takes { title }.
Renaming a document changes only the D1 title: it makes no revision and leaves the markdown's own heading unchanged.
GET /api/documents/:id/export?kind=prd is authorized by document.export and returns the current markdown as text/markdown with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<title-slug>.md"`.
Exporting a past revision with ?revision= additionally requires the document.history policy.
Importing a file reads its bytes in the browser and sends them as the markdown field.
An imported file must be UTF-8 and at most 5 MiB.
Workspace find searches document titles only.
Browser routes carry the workspace and the document as `/w/<workspaceId>/d/<documentId>-<title-slug>`, followed by the link steps of spec.contract.links.
The title slug is ignored when a browser path is read.
A wrong title slug is replaced with the canonical one, so a renamed PRD's old address still opens it.
A workspaceId that is not the document's own gives the same 404 as an unknown document.
Section and task IDs may repeat across PRDs, because every lookup is scoped to one document.

sections.title: Members and invitations
sections.summary: Builds the hosted API for workspace members and per-document guests: listing members, inviting by email, changing roles, removing members, sharing a single PRD with a guest, and accepting single-use, address-bound invitation tokens. Guests can reach only the documents shared with them and get 404 everywhere else in the workspace.

requirements.text: `GET /api/workspaces/:id/members`, under policy `workspace.read`, returns the workspace's members with their roles, and also returns pending invitations when the caller is an admin or owner.
`POST /api/workspaces/:id/invitations`, under policy `workspace.manageMembers`, takes `{ email, role }`, reserves a `members` seat and emails an invitation link.
`DELETE /api/workspaces/:id/invitations/:inv`, under policy `workspace.manageMembers`, revokes a pending invitation and releases its seat.
`PATCH /api/workspaces/:id/members/:user`, under policy `workspace.manageMembers`, changes a member's role.
The last owner of a workspace must not be demoted or removed.

`DELETE /api/workspaces/:id/members/:user`, under policy `workspace.manageMembers`, removes the membership and the person's grants in that workspace, revokes their agents for it, and releases the seat, all through `revoke`.
Removing a member takes away all their access to the workspace's PRDs; a manager can restore access to one only by sharing it with them again as a guest.

`POST /api/documents/:id/invitations`, under policy `document.manage`, takes `{ email, access }` where access is `read` or `comment`, checks the `guestsPerPrd` entitlement and emails an invitation link.
A document invitation to an email that belongs to a workspace member is refused with `Already a member. Set their access in Share.`
`PUT /api/documents/:id/grants/:user`, under policy `document.manage`, sets a member's or guest's grant on the document.
A guest's grant on a document is capped at `comment`.
`PUT /api/documents/:id/member-access`, under policy `document.manage`, sets the document's `memberAccess`.
`DELETE /api/documents/:id/grants/:user`, under policy `document.manage`, removes the grant through `revoke`.
`GET /api/documents/:id/access`, under policy `document.manage`, returns who can read, comment, edit or manage the document and why: role, member access, grant or public.
Each invitation is bound to one person and one scope (a workspace or a single document).
An invitation link holds a 32-byte random token encoded as base64url.
Only the SHA-256 hash of an invitation token is stored, never the token itself.
An invitation token expires seven days after it is issued.
An invitation token can be used only once.
`POST /api/invitations/:token/accept` requires a signed-in user whose confirmed email equals the invitation's email, compared case-insensitively.
Any other user accepting an invitation gets `403` with `This invitation was sent to another address.`, and the response does not name the invited address.
Accepting a workspace invitation adds the person to the workspace with the invitation's role.
Accepting a document invitation adds a grant on that one document only.
Knowing a private PRD's address must not grant any access to it.
A guest sees the documents shared with them under "Shared with you", served by `/api/me`.
For a guest, every workspace route and every other document of that workspace returns `404`, identical to the response for an unknown ID.

sections.title: Agent credentials and gate approvals
sections.summary: Builds agent identities with their own revocable, scoped credentials whose access follows their delegating person, the progress-event endpoint that records events with a server-set actor, and person-only gate approvals tied to the PRD, spec and plan revisions current at the time.

requirements.text: An agent has its own identity, separate from the person it acts for, and its own scoped credential that can be revoked.
POST /api/workspaces/:id/agents (agent.create) takes { name, scope } and returns the Agent and its token exactly once, in the form cagt_<agent id without prefix>_<32 random bytes, base64url>.
Only the SHA-256 of an agent token's secret is stored; the secret itself is not.
GET /api/workspaces/:id/agents lists the caller's own agents, and admins and owners see every agent in the workspace.
DELETE /api/workspaces/:id/agents/:agent sets the agent's revoked_at and runs revoke for the agent's scope.
A request carrying an agent token resolves to an agent principal.
The agent token's secret is compared in constant time.
An agent's last_used_at is updated at most once a minute.
A request with a revoked or unknown agent token gets 401 unauthenticated with the message "This agent's credential was revoked or is unknown."
An agent's access is checked on every request against its delegating person's current access, so that when that person loses access the agent loses it too without any further revocation.
Agents must never count as members of a workspace.
POST /api/documents/:id/events (progress.write) takes { events: Array<{ id: EventId; event: Event }> } with at most 500 events per request.
The room stores each progress event with a new ID and broadcasts it.
A progress event whose ID the room already holds is skipped.
The server sets each progress event's actor from the principal: agent:<agentId> for an agent and human:<name> for a person.
A progress line from an agent that claims a human: actor is refused with 403.
An agent's done event on a gated task is stored as it is, and status derivation does not treat it as an approval.
POST /api/documents/:id/tasks/:task/approve (gate.approve) takes { clientId }.
A gate approval is refused with 409 unless the latest trace snapshot shows the task blocked_on_human.

On a gate approval the room records a GateApproval with the inputs it applies to (the current PRD and spec revisions, the latest plan record and the task's newest commit in the snapshot) and broadcasts approval.
A gate approval from an agent gets 403 "Only a person can approve a gate.", whatever its delegating person could do.
An approval is tied to revision IDs, not content; an edit or a restore of an older revision makes a new revision ID, and an approval of an earlier revision never carries over to it.
The viewer shows the difference between the revisions an approval applies to and the current revisions.

The agent token is returned only once and only the SHA-256 of its secret is stored.
An agent's access is derived on every request from its delegating person's current access instead of being granted separately.
decisions.why: When that person loses access, so does the agent, with nothing more to revoke.

decisions.text: Agents never count as members.
The server sets a progress event's actor from the principal rather than trusting the actor the line claims.
An agent's done on a gated task is stored but not treated as an approval.
Only a person can approve a gate; an agent cannot, whatever its delegating person could do.
An approval is tied to revision IDs rather than to content, so it never carries over to a new revision, including a restore of an older one.

sections.title: Visibility
sections.summary: Builds whole-PRD public/private visibility for the hosted service: the visibility-change route and its side effects, an FTS5 search table of public documents, server-rendered public pages with SEO metadata, discovery routes (explore, search API, sitemap, robots), and a redacted public view of plan traces, with private documents hidden from every anonymous surface.

requirements.text: Sharing applies to a whole PRD, not to parts of it.
A public PRD is openly public, not protected by a secret link.
A private PRD exists only for the people the access policy lets in.
Changing a document's visibility is done with PATCH /api/documents/:id/visibility and requires the document.manage permission.
A request to make a document public is { visibility: "public", acknowledged: true }, sent after the sharing dialog's explanation; a request without acknowledged is refused.
Making a document public reserves the publicPrds entitlement and releases the privatePrds entitlement.
Making a document public inserts the document's title and the visible text of its current PRD into the public search table.
When a document's visibility changes to public, the room broadcasts a visibility message.
Making a document private writes private to D1 first, before the other steps.
Making a document private must never fail because of the private PRD allowance; the workspace may go over that allowance, which only blocks creating new private PRDs.
Making a document private deletes its row from the public search table.
Making a document private runs revoke for the anonymous principal, closing every anonymous socket for the document with close code 4410.
A new D1 migration creates the virtual table public_search using fts5(document_id unindexed, title, body).
Only public documents have rows in the public_search table.
Each accepted save of a public PRD replaces that document's row in the public_search table.
The visible text indexed for search is derived with mdast-util-from-markdown, leaving out code fences and HTML comments.
GET /w/:ws/d/:doc[-slug]/* is answered by render/page.ts, which returns the viewer's page for a document the request may read.

For a public document, the page also contains the server-rendered current PRD in an <article> element and its threads as a plain list, with the markdown rendered to a string through the viewer's renderMarkdown, the same way the docs site prerenders its pages.

A public document's page head contains <title>, meta name=description (the first paragraph, at most 160 characters), og:title, og:description, og:url, og:type set to article, og:image (the operator's configured image), twitter:card and link rel=canonical.
For any document the request may not read, the page route returns the same "Not available" page with <meta name="robots" content="noindex"> and no title, text or count from the document.
An authorized reader of a private document gets the viewer page without server-rendered content and with noindex, and the viewer loads the rest through the API.
GET /explore and GET /api/public/documents?q= list public PRDs, newest change first, with search through the full-text public_search table.
GET /sitemap.xml lists public PRDs from D1 as it is at request time.
GET /robots.txt allows /w/ and /explore.
The explore, public search, and sitemap routes must not be able to list a private PRD; they read only public rows.
publicTraceOf(trace) produces what anonymous readers get from a plan snapshot, keeping the spec, the tasks with their statuses, model and reasoning, and the stacks.

publicTraceOf removes commits (keeping only a count), session IDs, files and worktrees, path: gate reasons (keeping required), event detail, and every private field defined by spec.contract.usage-in-the-trace.
Code, agent transcripts and repository access must never be part of a public PRD.
Every document and export route enforces document.read.
History is guarded by document.history, which the public access floor never grants.
Comments are served with the document and filtered the same way as the document.
Link previews expose metadata only for public documents.
Anonymous live-update sockets are allowed only while a document is public and are closed with code 4410 when it becomes private.
There are no attachments at launch.
An earlier revision of a public PRD returns 404 to anonymous readers.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.summary: Builds document discussion in the hosted room: durable threads, replies, comment edits and resolution behind policy-checked HTTP routes, plus core's pure `anchorStateOf`, which reports whether a thread's anchor is still attached to the current revision or has changed.

requirements.text: Threads, replies and resolution live in the room, which stores them durably in the `threads` and `comments` tables.
`POST /api/documents/:id/threads` requires `document.comment` and takes `{ anchor, body, clientId }`.
Starting a thread requires that the anchor's revision exists.
Starting a thread with an anchor on an earlier revision also requires `document.history`.
When the anchor has a quote, the quote must be found in that revision's section, or the request is rejected with `invalid-input`.
`POST /api/documents/:id/threads/:root/replies` requires `document.comment` and takes `{ body, clientId }`.
`PATCH /api/documents/:id/comments/:note` is allowed only for the comment's author and takes `{ version, body }`.
A comment edit whose version is not the current one gets `stale-comment` together with the current comment.
`POST /api/documents/:id/threads/:root/resolve` and `/reopen` require `thread.resolve`.
An agent may resolve only its own threads and is refused on a person's thread.
A person may resolve anyone's thread.
`GET /api/documents/:id/threads` requires `document.read` and returns every `ThreadView`, open and resolved.
`GET /api/documents/:id/threads/:root` requires `document.read` and returns one thread.
Every comment has an authenticated `Author`, set from the principal.
Comment bodies are markdown and are rendered through `renderMarkdown`, which writes no raw HTML.
A comment's link is the document's route followed by `/note/<id>`, and the viewer opens that link on the comment's thread.
Two replies sent at once each get their own ID and `seq`, and both are kept.
Comments inherit the document's visibility (a public PRD's comments are public), and an anchor creates no visibility rule of its own.
`anchorStateOf(current, anchor)` in `packages/core/src/anchors.ts` is pure.
An anchor on the current revision is attached.
An anchor on an earlier revision is attached when its section still exists in the current markdown and its quote, when it has one, is still found there.
An anchor on an earlier revision whose section or quote is no longer found is changed, with reason `section-missing` or `passage-changed`.
The anchor text match uses the rule `passageOf` uses: the section's visible text joined with one space, whitespace collapsed, and an exact, case-sensitive match.
Visible text for anchor matching comes from `mdast-util-from-markdown` with GFM, in core.
The server fills a changed anchor's `original` only for a reader allowed `document.history`.
A reader without `document.history`, including the public reader, must not see any of the earlier revision's text; they see only that the anchor changed (`original: null`).
A thread must never be deleted because its anchored text changed.
A request retried with the same `clientId` returns the same comment rather than creating a new one.

Two concurrent replies are both kept, and two edits of one comment from the same version give the second `stale-comment`.
An agent resolves its own thread and is refused when resolving a person's thread.
A request retried with the same `clientId` returns the same comment.
`anchors-agree.test.ts` runs core's `anchorStateOf` and the viewer's `passageOf` on shared fixtures and finds they give the same answer.

decisions.text: Comments inherit the document's visibility; an anchor creates no visibility rule of its own.
A changed anchor's earlier text (`original`) is shown only to readers allowed `document.history`; everyone else, including public readers, sees only that it changed.
A thread is kept, marked changed, rather than deleted when its anchored text changes.
Core's anchor matching reuses the viewer's `passageOf` rule (visible text joined with one space, whitespace collapsed, exact case-sensitive match) so the two agree.
Agents may resolve only their own threads, while people may resolve anyone's.

sections.title: Links between PRDs
sections.summary: Adds links between PRDs written as markdown links with a `doc:<DocumentId>[#<SectionId>]` href: core extracts them, the hosted Worker stores them in a `document_links` table on each save and serves access-checked `links` and `backlinks` routes, and the viewer renders resolved links, "No access" chips and a backlinks list.

requirements.text: A PRD links to another PRD with an ordinary markdown link whose href is `doc:<DocumentId>` or `doc:<DocumentId>#<SectionId>`.
The editor inserts a link to another PRD from a picker of the PRDs the author can read.
Export keeps a `doc:` link's href exactly as it is written.
A link between PRDs must not grant any access to the target document.
A link between PRDs must not imply a task dependency.
`docLinksOf(markdown)` in core is pure and returns each `doc:` link outside fences as `{ target, section }`.
On each accepted save of a PRD, the Worker replaces that document's rows in `document_links` with rows built from the new current revision.
`GET /api/documents/:id/links` requires `document.read` and asks `decide` about every link target for the caller.

For each target, `GET /api/documents/:id/links` returns either `{ href, state: "readable", title, sectionTitle, excerpt }` with the excerpt at most 160 characters, or `{ href, state: "unavailable" }`.
`GET /api/documents/:id/backlinks` requires `document.read` and returns only the source documents the caller can read, with their title and section.
`GET /api/documents/:id/backlinks` must not include sources the caller cannot read, nor a count of them.
The markdown renderer receives the resolved link map through a `docLink` hook.
A readable link target renders as a link to the target document's route, with the document's title as a tooltip.
An unavailable link target keeps the author's link text followed by a chip reading "No access", showing no title, excerpt or status.
The public page and `/explore` call the same links and backlinks routes as an anonymous principal.
The search table must never hold another document's title.
`backlinksView` lists the backlinks under the PRD pane's last section.

sections.title: Data sources
sections.summary: Builds the viewer's build-time data source selection: a `__CAIRN_SOURCE__` set from the Vite mode (demo, local or hosted), one loader per source in `load.ts` with no fallback between them, and bundles in which the demo trace appears only in the demo build.

requirements.text: The viewer's data source is chosen once, when the viewer is built, and is never inferred at runtime.
vite.config.ts sets __CAIRN_SOURCE__ from the build mode: --mode demo, local or hosted.
A viewer build run without one of the modes demo, local or hosted fails.
The viewer never reads import.meta.env.PROD to choose a data source.
Each data source has its own loader in load.ts.
The demo loader loads demo-trace.json once.
The local loader polls /api/trace.
The hosted loader loads the workspace and document APIs.
A failed load shows its error above whatever the viewer last loaded, or shows the error alone when nothing has been loaded.
No loader ever falls back to another data source.
demo-trace.json is imported only behind the condition __CAIRN_SOURCE__ === "demo", so that the local and hosted bundles do not contain it.
apps/site builds the viewer in demo mode.
cairn serve serves the local build of the viewer.
The hosted Worker serves the hosted build of the viewer.

sections.title: Workspace screens
sections.summary: Builds the hosted viewer's screens around the existing reader: sign-in, workspace switcher, PRD list, empty states, limit notes, the markdown editor with stale-save handling, revision history with restore, and live updates over the document's socket.

requirements.text: Every hosted screen uses the design system's pieces.
Signed out, the `/` route shows the sign-in screen offering GitHub, Google and email sign-in, each only as the operator turned it on.
Signed in, the `/` route redirects to the last workspace, or to the personal workspace.
The `/w/<ws>` route shows the workspace's PRD list with a title filter, "New PRD" and "Import markdown", and "Members" for managers.
The `/w/<ws>/d/<doc>-<slug>/<link steps>` route shows the reader for one PRD with a document bar holding Edit, History, Share, Export and the comment count.
Link steps in the document route are read through `linkRoute`, nested under the `/w/<ws>/d/<doc>-<slug>` prefix.
The `/w/<ws>/d/<doc>/edit` route shows the editor.
The `/w/<ws>/d/<doc>/history` route shows the history list, and `/w/<ws>/d/<doc>/history/<rev>` shows one earlier revision.
The `/shared` route shows "Shared with you" for guests.
The `/explore` route shows public discovery.
The top bar holds a workspace switcher listing the personal workspace, each team workspace, "Shared with you" and "New team workspace…".
"New team workspace…" asks for a name and calls `POST /api/workspaces`.
A workspace with no PRDs shows "Write a PRD" and "Import markdown", one sentence on what a PRD is, and a link to the getting started page.
A PRD with no plan shows only the PRD pane, full width, with no status lines.
Beside the PRD pane of a PRD with no plan is a card headed "Connect implementation" with the `cairn connect <this page's address>` command to copy and a link to its docs page.
The hosted build never shows the demo's plan.
The "New PRD", "Import markdown" and "Invite" buttons read the workspace's entitlements.

When the next action would not fit the workspace's limits, the button opens a note naming the limit (such as `This workspace has 3 of 3 PRDs on Free.`), with "Upgrade" for owners, before any request is sent.
The editor is a monospace `textarea` with a "Preview" toggle that renders through `renderMarkdown`.
The editor edits the PRD, or the spec when the document has one.
The editor's Model holds `draft`, `base` and `isSaving`.
The draft is saved to `localStorage` under `<document>:<kind>:<base>`, at most once a second, so a reload keeps it.
A successful save clears the draft from `localStorage`.
Save sends `base` with a new `clientId`.
A stale save keeps the draft and shows a banner such as `Someone saved revision 7 while you were editing. Your draft is still here.` offering "Show their version", "Copy my draft" and "Save over it".
"Show their version" opens a read-only copy of the current revision beside the draft.
"Copy my draft" copies the draft.
"Save over it" takes the current revision (e.g. 7) as the base and saves the draft as the next revision (e.g. 8); the overwritten revision stays in history.
Leaving the editor with an unsaved draft asks first.
The history list shows each revision's number, author, time and "restored from N".
Opening a revision from history shows it in the reader, read-only, under a banner such as `Revision 2 of 5, by Ada, 3 Nov`.
"Restore" requires the `edit` permission.
"Restore" asks with `This adds a new revision with this text. Comments, tasks and sharing do not change.` and then calls `restore`.
While a document is open, `live.ts` keeps its socket and applies `RoomMessage`s by `seq`.
When the document socket opens, `live.ts` fetches `state`.
A `revision` message from someone else while the editor is open shows a notice such as `Revision 7 was saved by Ada` and leaves the draft alone.
An `access: "none"` message clears the document from the Model and shows "You no longer have access to this PRD.".

Importing "Roadmap" adds it to the list; it can be renamed, opened, edited and exported, and has comments and Share; the reader shows no spec or stacks pane and shows the "Connect implementation" card.

decisions.text: The hosted build never shows the demo's plan; a PRD with no plan shows only the PRD pane plus a "Connect implementation" card.

The editor's draft is kept in localStorage, written at most once a second.

decisions.text: A stale save keeps the draft and lets the person choose to view theirs, copy the draft, or save over it; saving over is an explicit overwrite that adds a new revision while the overwritten revision stays in history.
Restore adds a new revision with the earlier text rather than rewriting history; comments, tasks and sharing do not change.
A revision saved by someone else while the editor is open is announced but leaves the draft alone.

sections.title: Workspace settings
sections.summary: Builds the hosted viewer's workspace settings screens: the Members page (members, roles, invitations, removal), the Agents page (listing, creating and revoking agent credentials), and the `/invite/<token>` invitation acceptance page.

requirements.text: Workspace settings are served at `/settings/w/<ws>/members` and `/settings/w/<ws>/agents`.
The Members page lists each member of the workspace with their role, and lists pending invitations, each with a "Revoke" action.
Owners and admins see an "Invite by email" control on the Members page, with a choice of role of member or admin.
Owners and admins see a role menu and a "Remove" action on each member row.
"Remove" asks for confirmation before removing a member, with the text `They lose access to this workspace's PRDs at once, including in tabs they have open.`
Members (non-admin, non-owner) see the Members list read-only, without invite, role or remove controls.
Guests must not reach the Members page: the API responds `404` and the screen shows "Not available".
The Agents page lists the caller's own agents, or every agent in the workspace for admins and owners, each showing its delegating person, scope, last use and a "Revoke" action.
"New agent" asks for a name, the PRDs the agent may act on (chosen from those the person can read) and the agent's actions.
After creating an agent, the screen shows the agent's token once only, with `cairn connect agent` instructions and the note `Agents cannot approve gates.`
The invitation page at `/invite/<token>` asks a signed-out person to sign in first.
After sign-in, the invitation page shows what the invitation grants and an "Accept" action.
Any refusal on the invitation page is shown in the API's own words.

sections.title: Sharing dialog
sections.summary: Builds the "Share" dialog for a PRD: it explains who can access the document and why, lets managers invite guests and change or remove access, and makes changing visibility to public or private a two-step confirmation that spells out what is exposed or what cannot be recalled.

requirements.text: "Share" opens a dialog with role="dialog" that explains who can do what with the PRD, using the data from GET /api/documents/:id/access.
The dialog shows the member access as a line such as "Everyone in Acme can edit.", with a menu on that line for managers.
The dialog lists each person with a grant, labelled "member" or "guest", with their access level and the reason they have it: owner, admin, member access or invited.
The dialog lists pending guest invitations.
The dialog shows the visibility as "Private. Only the people above can open it." or "Public. Anyone with the address, and search engines, can read it."
Managers get "Invite a guest", with an email field and a choice of only "Can read" or "Can comment".
Managers get a level menu and a "Remove" control on each person in the list.
People without the manage permission see the access explanation read-only, with no controls.

Making a PRD public is two steps: "Make public…" first shows what becomes public: the current text of the PRD; its comments, resolved ones included, and their authors' names; and the spec, the tasks and their statuses.
The make-public confirmation step says what stays private: earlier revisions, code, agent transcripts and repository access, and the people who have access.
Only the "Make public" button in the confirmation step sends the visibility change with acknowledged: true; no request is sent before it.

Making a PRD private is two steps: "Make private…" says that signed-out visitors lose access at the next load, that the PRD leaves Cairn's discovery and search at once, and that copies others have made and search engines' caches cannot be recalled at once.
After the make-private change is confirmed, the dialog shows the visibility as "Private".

Making a PRD private also takes two steps, with a confirmation that external copies and search caches cannot be recalled at once.
Guests can be invited only with "Can read" or "Can comment", not edit access.
People without manage still see the full access explanation, read-only, rather than having the dialog hidden from them.

sections.title: Comments in the reader
sections.summary: Adds comment threads to the reader: starting a thread from a selected passage or a heading, markers on passages and headings with open threads, and a thread node in the detail panel that shows the anchor, comments and policy-allowed actions, kept live by `thread` messages from the room.

requirements.text: When a person with `comment` access selects a passage in the PRD or in a card's full section, a "Comment" action appears beside "Copy link to passage", using the `SelectedPassage` that `TrackSelection` already sends.
Each heading has a "Comment" action that comments on the whole section.
Both the passage and the heading "Comment" actions open a composer whose anchor holds the revision being read.
The passage of an open thread is wrapped in `mark[data-thread]` and shown with a dotted ink underline.
A heading shows `◆` followed by the number of its open threads (for example `◆ 2`).
Clicking a passage marker or a heading's thread count opens the thread.
A thread is a new kind of node in the detail panel's trail, opened by a marker, the comment count or a `/note/<id>` link.
The thread view shows its anchor: the section's title and the quoted text.

When a thread's anchor has changed, the thread view shows `The text this was about has changed.`, followed by the original quote when `original` is present, or by `It was about an earlier revision you can't open.` otherwise.
Each comment in the thread view shows the author's name with "person" or "agent", the time and the body.
Each comment has a "Copy link" action that copies its `/note/<id>` link.
Each comment shows an "Edit" action to its author.
The thread view offers Reply, Resolve and Reopen only as far as policy allows.
A failed send keeps the text in the composer.
On a `stale-comment` result, the view shows the current text beside the person's edit.
For a signed-out reader on a public PRD, threads are read-only and end with "Sign in to comment".
`thread` messages from the room update the detail panel and the markers.

Threads are shown as a new kind of node in the existing detail panel trail rather than in a separate view.

sections.title: `cairn connect`
sections.summary: Builds the `cairn connect` CLI commands that link one repo's `.cairn/` directory to one hosted PRD: signing in, storing credentials and agent tokens, and a four-step sync (documents, events, plan, approvals) that never overwrites unsynced local text.

requirements.text: `cairn connect <address>` takes a PRD's address as copied from the browser and reads the origin, the workspace and the document from it.
When the machine holds no session for the address's origin, `cairn connect <address>` signs in with device authorization: it prints the code and the address and waits.

`cairn connect <address>` writes `.cairn/connect.json` as `{ version: 1, origin, workspaceId, documentId, prd: { revision, hash }, spec: { revision, hash } | null, approvalsSeen: Array<string> }`, through the PRD's current revision.
After writing `.cairn/connect.json`, `cairn connect <address>` runs a first sync.
When `git remote get-url origin` returns a URL, `cairn connect <address>` records the repo's remote URL in `connections`.
`cairn connect agent <name> [--actions progress,comment]` creates an agent for this PRD using the person's session and stores the agent's token.
Credentials are stored in `~/.config/cairn/credentials.json`, or `%APPDATA%\cairn\credentials.json` on Windows, with file mode 0600.
The credentials file holds, for each origin, a person's session and named agent tokens.
Credentials are never stored in the repo.
When `CAIRN_AGENT_TOKEN` is set in the environment, it is used in place of the stored agent token.
`cairn connect sync` runs four steps in order: documents, events, plan and approvals.
`cairn connect sync --watch` runs the four steps again whenever `.cairn/` changes, debounced by one second.

The document step covers `prd.md` and, once it exists, `spec.md`; a file is changed locally when its hash differs from `connect.json`, and changed remotely when the hosted current revision differs from `connect.json`.
When neither the local file nor the remote document has changed, the document step does nothing for that file.
When only the local file changed, the document step saves it with `base` set to the recorded revision and records the result in `connect.json`.
When only the remote document changed, the document step writes the hosted markdown to the local file atomically and records it in `connect.json`.

When both the local file and the remote document changed, or a save comes back stale, the document step leaves the local file as it is, writes the hosted version to `.cairn/prd.hosted.md` (or `spec.hosted.md`), prints `Both .cairn/prd.md and the hosted PRD changed since the last sync. Merge them, then run cairn connect sync.`, and exits 1.
No sync step overwrites unsynced local text.
In the events step, each line of `events.jsonl` has as its ID the SHA-256 of its bytes.
The events step sends lines in batches of 500, authenticated with the agent's token when there is one and the person's session otherwise.
The room skips event IDs it has already stored, so resending after a drop or a rewrite of `events.jsonl` adds nothing.
When `manifest.json` exists, the plan step uploads `buildTrace` with its private fields left out, together with the plan record's inputs.
The plan step skips the upload when the trace's hash has not changed.
After a plan upload, the room broadcasts `trace`.

For each hosted `GateApproval` not in `approvalsSeen`, the approvals step appends `{ status: "done", actor: "human:<name>", detail: "approved in <origin> against PRD revision <n>" }` with `appendEvent`, then records the approval in `approvalsSeen`.
The local orchestrator and derivation treat an approval appended by the approvals step the same as one from `cairn approve`.
A `401` on an agent token prints `This agent's credential was revoked. Run cairn connect agent <name> again.`, exits 1, and leaves local files unchanged.
A `404` prints `This PRD is not available to you.` and exits 1.

Against the hosted Worker, a sync where both `prd.md` and the hosted PRD changed leaves `prd.md` byte for byte unchanged.
Against the hosted Worker, 3,000 events sent twice are stored once.
Against the hosted Worker, an agent's events land in the PRD named in `connect.json`.
Against the hosted Worker, after the agent is revoked, the next sync exits 1 with the revoked-credential message.
Against the hosted Worker, an approval made in the room is appended locally exactly once, and `cairn status` then shows the task `done`.

On a conflict the sync keeps the local file and writes the hosted version beside it for the person to merge, rather than merging or overwriting.

Hosted approvals are brought in as ordinary local events appended with `appendEvent`.

decisions.text: The uploaded build trace leaves out its private fields.
`--watch` is the mode an orchestrator leaves running, debounced by one second.
Tests run against the hosted Worker in the test pool.

sections.title: Plan source
sections.summary: Records which PRD a plan was made from: `cairn plan` writes the PRD's SHA-256 into the manifest, the hosted room matches it to a PRD revision once when the plan is uploaded, and the viewer warns when the plan or an approval was made against an older PRD revision or an unsynced local draft.

requirements.text: `Manifest` gains an optional field `source` of shape `{ prd: Sha256Hex }`.
A manifest without `source` still decodes.
`cairn plan` writes the SHA-256 of `prd.md`'s bytes, as they stood when the plan ran, into `source.prd` on every write of the manifest.
Recording the plan source must not change any task or change how planning works.
`POST /api/documents/:id/plan` requires the `plan.write` permission and takes the trace snapshot together with the manifest's hash and source.
On a plan upload the room stores the trace snapshot.
On a plan upload the room stores a `PlanRecord` whose `prdRevision` is the newest PRD revision whose hash equals `source.prd`, or `null` when no PRD revision has that text.
The stored `PlanRecord`'s `specRevision` is the current spec revision at upload.
The PRD revision match is made once, at upload; a later restore of the same PRD text does not change the record's `prdRevision`.
`GET /api/documents/:id/plan` requires the `document.read` permission and returns the latest snapshot, in its public form for anonymous readers, and the latest `PlanRecord`.

When the plan record's `prdRevision` is not the current PRD revision, the viewer shows over the spec pane `Plan made from revision 4. The PRD is now at revision 6.` (with the actual revision numbers) and a link to that revision in history.
When the plan record's `prdRevision` is `null`, the viewer shows over the spec pane `Plan made from a local draft that was never synced.`
When the plan record's `prdRevision` matches the current PRD revision, the viewer shows no plan-source notice.

An approval whose `prdRevision` is not the current PRD revision reads `Approved against PRD revision 4, before the latest edits.` (with the actual revision number) in the task detail.
A stale plan or approval must not trigger any replanning or restacking.

sections.title: Billing
sections.summary: Bills each workspace through Stripe: a D1 migration for subscriptions and processed webhook events, checkout and customer-portal routes, an idempotent webhook handler that sets subscription state from the latest Stripe object, a mapping from Stripe status to entitlements, and a billing settings screen.

requirements.text: Billing is attached to the workspace: the workspace is the entity that is billed.
Stripe is used through the `stripe` package with its fetch HTTP client and its asynchronous webhook verification, so that it runs on Workers.
The implementer reads the `stripe` package's declarations before writing `stripe.ts`.
A new D1 migration adds the `subscriptions` and `billing_events` tables.

`POST /api/workspaces/:id/billing/checkout`, under the `workspace.billing` policy, takes `{ plan, seats }` with seats at least the workspace's current member count, and returns a Stripe Checkout Session URL in subscription mode that carries the workspace ID.
`POST /api/workspaces/:id/billing/portal`, under the `workspace.billing` policy, returns a Stripe Customer Portal URL for payment methods, seats, invoices and cancellation.
`POST /api/billing/webhook` is authorized by the Stripe signature, and the handler verifies the signature before anything else.
The webhook handler inserts the event's ID into `billing_events` with `insert or ignore`; a duplicate event does nothing more.

For a new event, the handler fetches the subscription from Stripe rather than trusting the payload's order, and sets the `subscriptions` row from it: the plan from the price, the status, the seat count, the period end, `cancel_at_period_end`, and `stripe_updated` from the subscription's own timestamp.
The handler skips the write when the stored `stripe_updated` is newer than the fetched subscription's.
Subscription state must not be incremented; it is always set from the latest Stripe object, so a duplicate or delayed event cannot add capacity.

A Stripe status of `active` or `trialing` maps to entitlement status `active`, or `canceling` when the subscription is set to cancel at period end, with the paid plan's limits and `members` set to the seats.
A Stripe status of `past_due` maps to entitlement status `past_due`, keeping the paid limits until `grace_ends_at`, which is the first failed payment plus `graceDays`.

A Stripe status of `canceled` or `unpaid`, or `past_due` after the grace period, maps to entitlement status `canceled` with the free plan's limits, and `overLimit` computed as in `spec.hosted-launch.entitlements`.
A paid plan's members limit is its seat count.
Seats are added in the Stripe Customer Portal.
Inviting a member past the seat count is refused with `limit-reached` naming `members`, so no seat is ever bought without the person choosing it.
No billing event publishes, unpublishes or deletes anything.
With billing off, the billing routes return `404`.
`billingView` at `/settings/w/<ws>/billing` shows the plan, status, seats, limits and usage.
`billingView` shows the grace date or the over-limit dimensions, with what each one blocks, and the text `Your PRDs stay as they are, and you can still export every one.`
For owners, `billingView` shows "Upgrade", which goes to checkout, and "Manage or cancel billing", which goes to the portal.
Billing tests run against recorded Stripe fixtures and a stub HTTP client.

A Scene test of the "New PRD" note at the limit shows the limit's name before any request is sent.

decisions.text: The workspace, not the user, is the billed entity.
For each new webhook event, fetch the subscription from Stripe instead of using the event payload.
decisions.why: So the handler does not depend on the order in which payloads arrive.

decisions.text: Subscription state is set from the latest Stripe object and never incremented.
decisions.why: So a duplicate or delayed event cannot add capacity.

decisions.text: Seats are added only in the Customer Portal; inviting past the seat count is refused with `limit-reached` and does not buy a seat automatically.
decisions.why: So no seat is ever bought without the person choosing it.

decisions.text: Billing events never publish, unpublish or delete anything.
Tests run against recorded Stripe fixtures and a stub HTTP client instead of live Stripe.

sections.title: Self-hosting
sections.summary: Makes the hosted Worker deployable by an operator in their own Cloudflare account from a settings schema, adds operator backup and restore routes, CLI commands and a weekly restore drill, and writes the hosted, self-hosting, backup and support docs.

requirements.text: The managed service and a self-hosted team deployment run the same Worker, policy and screens.
`config.ts` decodes the deployment's settings through a schema.
`CAIRN_DOMAIN` is the site's domain, and the email sender is a subdomain of it.
`CAIRN_STAGE` is a prefix for every Cloudflare resource name.
`CAIRN_AUTH` is a subset of `github`, `google` and `email`, and each enabled method needs its own secrets.
`CAIRN_BILLING` is `managed` or `off`; with `off` no Stripe secrets are needed and every workspace is put on the `self-hosted` entitlement.
`CAIRN_SOCIAL_IMAGE` sets the `og:image` URL, and `CAIRN_SUPPORT` sets the support address or URL that the site and the docs show.
`OPERATOR_TOKEN` is a secret that guards the admin routes.
An operator can deploy with `alchemy deploy` and these settings in their own Cloudflare account without a subscription to the managed service.
A deploy runs the D1 migrations, and each room runs its own migrations when it wakes.
`GET /api/admin/backup`, called with `Authorization: Bearer <OPERATOR_TOKEN>`, streams NDJSON starting with a header that carries the format version, the app version and the time.
The backup stream contains every D1 row except sessions and one-time tokens.
For each document, the backup stream contains the room's revisions with bodies inline (R2 bodies fetched), threads, comments, events, plan records, snapshots and approvals.
The backup stream ends with a trailer holding counts and the SHA-256 of every line before it.
`POST /api/admin/restore` takes a backup stream into a deployment whose D1 has no workspaces.
`POST /api/admin/restore` must not restore into a deployment whose D1 has any workspaces; it refuses it.
Restore checks the trailer, inserts the D1 rows, loads each room through an `import` RPC, and answers with the counts.
Restore keeps IDs, so addresses, links, anchors and approvals still resolve after it.
`cairn admin backup --origin <url> --out <file>` and `cairn admin restore --origin <url> --in <file>` call the backup and restore routes with `CAIRN_OPERATOR_TOKEN` from the environment.
A request to the admin routes with a wrong or missing token gets `404`.

The docs include short pages: hosted getting started (sign up, write or import a first PRD, invite people, share, connect a repo); self-hosting (Cloudflare setup, the settings, `alchemy deploy`, and upgrading); backup and restore; and support.
The self-hosting docs say that upgrading starts with taking a backup.
The support page gives the operator's support path, and for the managed service its support address and the issue tracker.
`restore-drill.yml` runs weekly and before each release.

The restore drill deploys a throwaway stage seeded through the API with PRDs, revisions, comments and a changed anchor, backs it up, deploys a second empty stage, restores into it and backs that up, compares the two backups' body hashes, and destroys both stages.
The managed service must not take customer work until the restore drill has passed once.
Editing `restore-drill.yml` is a change to a gated path and needs a person's approval.

sections.title: Launch acceptance
sections.summary: Defines the hosted release gates and the tests that check them. It covers two end-to-end acceptance flows in `launch.test.ts`, a cross-workspace isolation property test in `isolation.test.ts`, and a manual staging walkthrough plus a first-time operator self-host run recorded in `checklist.md`.

requirements.text: The launch acceptance tests run at the HTTP and WebSocket level in the Worker test pool.
Before release, a person walks through the release gates in a browser on staging, following checklist.md, and records the date and their name in it.
A new user can sign up by magic link without any checkout being called.
With no plan uploaded, a user can create a team workspace, create two PRDs (one written, one imported), and read, save, export and start a thread on each.
A guest invited as a commenter on one PRD can comment on that PRD.
For a PRD a guest was not invited to, the guest's GET, search, state and live requests each return 404, and that PRD does not appear in the guest's /api/me.
A signed-out visitor gets a public PRD's page with its title and og: tags, and can find the PRD in /explore.
Neither a public PRD's page nor its links shows a linked private PRD's title, an earlier revision, any commit or any session.
Once a public PRD is made private, a signed-out visitor who reloads it sees "Not available", and the PRD no longer appears in /explore.
On every route in the router's list, a request from a user of another workspace for a document or thread gets a response identical to the response for an unknown ID.
A socket upgrade from a user of another workspace is refused.
Before release, an operator who has never deployed Cairn follows the self-host guide in their own Cloudflare account, and the run is recorded in checklist.md.

They create a team workspace and two PRDs, one written and one imported, then read, save, export and start a thread on each with no plan uploaded. They invite a guest as a commenter on the first PRD. The guest comments on it. For the second PRD, the guest's GET, search, state and live each return 404, and the second PRD is absent from the guest's /api/me.

Flow 2 in launch.test.ts: a public PRD links to a private PRD and has an earlier revision. A signed-out visitor gets its page with its title and og: tags, and finds it in /explore. Neither the page nor links shows the private PRD's title, the earlier revision, any commit or any session. After the PRD is made private, the visitor's reload shows "Not available" and the PRD is not in /explore.

Operator run: before release, an operator who has never deployed Cairn follows the self-host guide in their own Cloudflare account, and the run is recorded in checklist.md. This sits alongside the restore test in spec.hosted-launch.self-hosting and the restore drill.

decisions.text: The acceptance tests in this section stay at the HTTP and WebSocket level. Screens are covered by the Scene tests named in each feature section, not by these tests.
Several release gates (revisions, agent credentials, billing, entitlements, self-hosting restore) are checked by tests in the sections that own them, not by new tests here.

sections.title: Refactors
sections.summary: Groups the refactors that make the code smaller without changing what it does, each with the pattern it uses and where that came from.

sections.title: Service factories
sections.summary: Adds the Recorder service factory and the shared test fixtures built beside it, and records the pattern in the Effect checklist.

requirements.text: `Recorder<Self, A>()(id)` returns a service class with `record`, `seen` and a static `layer` that provides it empty, and its return type is the `Recorder<Self, Id, A>` interface that extends `Context.ServiceClass`.
`Wire` and `Events` are declared with `Recorder` in one line each, and `Wire.client(answer)` gives the recording `HttpClient`.
`scriptedTerminal` and `stubPlanner` replace the copies in the plan tests and name their return types; an unscripted planner call dies with its name.
The Effect checklist has a services row for the factory and its annotation and a tests row for the shared fixtures.

decisions.text: The factory returns a class that extends a precomputed key, instead of `Object.assign` on the key.
decisions.why: The checklist rules out `Object.assign`, and `classSelfMismatch` refuses the inline `Context.Service` class.

sections.title: Optional services
sections.summary: Asks for the Judge with Effect.serviceOption in cairn plan and provides it only when it is configured, so the provided layer is the only switch for judging.

requirements.text: `Judge.whenConfigured(config)` is `Judge.live(config)` when `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or `judge.gatewayTokenEnv` is set, and `Layer.empty` otherwise; `cairn plan` provides it.
The judging checkpoints of `cairn plan` take the judge with `Effect.serviceOption(Judge)`, and without one print `JUDGING_SKIPPED` once and leave their input unjudged.
`unusedJudge` is removed and `plan` does not require `Judge`.
The Effect checklist has a services row for `Effect.serviceOption` and the choice of layer at the entry.

decisions.text: `unusedPlanner` and the `yield* Judge` of `cairn judge` stay.
decisions.why: Those runs cannot do without the service, so it stays a requirement the type checker enforces.

sections.title: Branching conversations
sections.summary: Gives each planner call its own Chat so a retry is a follow-up turn carrying only the error, and runs the splits of a refine round as branches of one trunk chat that holds the spec, with chat.ts's branch providing a copy of the current Chat through Effect.provideServiceEffect.

requirements.text: `branch` in `chat.ts` runs an effect with a new `Chat` made by `Chat.fromPrompt` from the current chat's history, provided with `Effect.provideServiceEffect`.
Each `Planner` call opens its own `Chat`, and a retry is a follow-up turn of it that carries only the error; `retry.md` holds only the error.
`withRetry` adds the prompt and the refused reply to the chat's history before asking again, because `Chat.generateObject` records nothing when decoding fails.

`Planner.splitTrunk(spec)` opens a chat with `split-task-opening.md` as one system message, and `refine.draftRounds` provides it once per round and runs each `splitTask(draft, reason)` in a `branch` of it.
The `cli` source keeps assistant turns when it flattens a prompt, marked `Your previous reply:`.
`effect/ai/Chat` is in the cli package's `allowedUnstableApis`, and the Effect checklist has a services row for branching a stateful service.

decisions.text: The judgments and `refineWith`'s `stack` `Ref` are not branched.
decisions.why: The judge holds no conversation, and the stack judgments are read and replaced by every round, so they stay one `Ref`.
